sec.h: Recipes made possible by species-specific materials
sec.x: Items butchered from animals or taken from traps are now named after their species (Names that show where an item came from), and 7 recipes that used to be impossible can now be made: Recipe / structure   Species-specific material it asks for Andrewsarchus Leather Rug   Andrewsarchus leather (dried, then tanned) Mini Compy Bean Bags (2 kinds)   Compsognathus leather ×15 · Compsognathus tooth ×5 Brachio Tooth Necklace   Brachio tooth (trimmed) Wolf Fur Hat   White wolf leather (dried then tanned — it stays white wolf leather) Tanning with White Sabertooth oil   White Sabertooth fat ×8 Inflammation Antidote   Root (from the Bird of Paradise) The meat of some animals works as the stamina ingredient of Mochi, Meat Skewers and Ginseng Chicken Soup · house parts (roof, wall, floor) crafted from materials with a known origin pass that origin on to the house, so the patterns on the house follow the material

[!tip] Product level is the average of every material — one low-level secondary material can drag the result down. [!tip] Plan your processing chain before you start — each item can only be processed 3 times (ore 5 · ordinary leather 4). [!tip] Long jobs like smelting and desulfurizing can be left at a kiln while you go gathering. [!tip] Before crafting a high-level item, open Expected Result — if the success rate is low, raise your Crafting Ability first (skills, food, gear, titles) or craft a lower-level version.

sec.h: Crafting and other actions can't overlap
sec.x: Starting another timed action (such as gathering or washing) while a craft is in progress cancels that craft, and its materials are not used · unattended crafting left on a workbench is not affected and keeps going · full rule on Gathering.

d: Latent and rare (green) attributes — how you get them while gathering, how they carry over when crafting, and what each one does

sec.x: Each material may come with attributes such as «Firm», «High Density», or green ones like «Black Sheen». When you craft, the attributes of the material in the main slot become attributes of the product — more attack, more durability, or special effects like bleeding. A sword with special attributes

Open Item Info for the item Attributes show as chips  with their level — the color tells how rare they are: Color   Meaning Green   Rare Attribute — a special effect Yellow   a good attribute Normal   a basic attribute Gray   a negative attribute Tap a chip to read its description · combat/gathering rare attributes have no number on the stats page — read the chip's description instead

When you gather, butcher or harvest a farm plot, each piece can get attributes in two ways: Source attributes — some sources always give fixed attributes (for example Mammoth leather is Oily) · the first (main) one gets +1 level for each point of the island's Unstable Index above 1 — the Index counts up to 6 on islands below level 60 and up to 8 on level 60 islands · an Index of 6 or higher only counts fully on a Flawless gather; otherwise it counts as Index 5 Random latent attributes — yellow · gray · green are rolled separately, so one piece can get several colors at once, with no limit on the number · none of this depends on your skills or the island's Index Color   Chance per piece   Level Yellow (good)   12.5% · farm plot products 50%   4 Gray (negative)   about 5.4% (3/7 of the yellow chance) · only for materials that have a gray pair   5 Green (rare)   bare hands 0.1% · holding a Lv30 tool 0.2% · Lv60 0.3% · butchering a big animal ×2   1 Multipliers — the «Secrets of Gathering» attribute on the tool you are holding (worn gear doesn't count), and titles/clan research with «Latent/Rare Attribute Rate», multiply the chance of all 3 colors by (1 + the total) · up to 100% per color Farm plots — the Lv20 encyclopedia mastery multiplies only the color you choose ×1.2 (yellow 50% → 60%, or green 0.1% → 0.12%) · green from farms exists only for flower, fruit, grain and other edible products · edible vegetables, mushrooms, sugarcane, coffee and so on roll 1 of the 3 food greens

On a Flawless gather, butcher or harvest, some materials get special effects (for the chance of a Flawless result see Success and failure): Material   Effect on a Flawless result Ordinary leather   +1 processing chance · gets «High Durability» 1 and «Flexibility» 1 Pelt (furred hide)   gets «High Durability» 1 (no extra processing chance) Armor leather   +3 processing chances · gets «High Durability» 1 and «Flexibility» 3 Ore   +1 processing chance · gets «Flexibility» 1 · becomes a «Big Chunk» instead of a «Chunk» Cotton from farms   gets «High Durability» 7 Flax from farms (tropical flax too)   gets «High Durability» 7 and «Tough» 7 Starting processing chances of materials: ore 5 · ordinary leather 4 · everything else 3 (pelt and armor leather 3) — so Flawless ore has 6, ordinary leather 5 and armor leather 6 (more in Crafting) Made a mistake while gathering (you still get the item — see Success and failure) gets «Low Durability» level 2, and ore, ordinary leather and armor leather lose 1 processing chance (ore falls to 4 · ordinary leather to 3 · armor leather to 2) Flawless no longer boosts the durability of gathered items, and no longer adds levels to yellow attributes A Flawless craft also gives the product an extra processing chance — see Crafting

The main part decides the product Only the material in the main slot passes attributes on Nothing is rolled away any more — at every crafting step (including steps whose product is a part: blade, string, plank …) every attribute the product type accepts carries over, and there is no «attributes were lost» message · attributes can only be missing in 3 cases: the average is below 1 · they weren't in the main slot · the product type doesn't accept that attribute Several pieces in the main slot: Yellow/gray/normal attributes — the product's level = the sum of the levels over all pieces in the main slot ÷ the number of pieces, rounded down (a piece without that attribute counts as 0) · a result of 0 = not carried over Green attributes — one piece in the main slot is enough (no averaging) · the same green attribute never stacks Titles and «Secrets of Gathering» have no effect when crafting (they only work when gathering) Processing recipes (trimming, smelting, tanning and so on) keep every attribute · a Flawless processing gives the attributes the recipe adds +1 level · a processing mistake gives 1 level less on the attributes the recipe adds (never below the item's own level) There is no limit on how many attributes can carry over The Expected Result window for crafting/building shows the attributes the product will have and their levels before you start — yellow and gray match the real result, while rare attributes that are picked 1-of-2 when the craft finishes show as «???» Exam

Once the product is a real item type, material attributes turn into product attributes — the value per level is below (gray attributes give the opposite effect with the same number): Product   Material attribute   Becomes   Per level Weapon   Firm   Attack Buff   +3.33 Weapon   High Density   Durability Buff   +10 Weapon   Lightweight   Accuracy Buff   +4.5 (+0.45% to hit) Weapon   Compact Structure   Lethality Buff   +0.67% critical chance Weapon   Pointy   Penetration Buff   +10 Weapon   Sharp Section   damage to animal body parts   +10% Weapon   Full   Stun Rate Buff   +1% Tool   Firm · Compact Structure · Lightweight · High Density   Attack · Lethality · Accuracy · Durability Buff   same as weapons Tool   Pointy   Crafting Ability Buff (all kinds)   +1 Tool   Sharp Section   Gathering Ability Buff (all kinds)   +1 Tool   Full   Building Ability Buff   +1 Clothes / accessories   Tough Fiber   Defense Buff   +2 Clothes / accessories   High Density   Durability Buff   +10 Clothes / accessories   Lightweight   Evasion Buff   +1.5 Clothes / accessories   Thin · Good Breathability · Oily Liquid · Fluffy   Heat · Humidity · Wind · Cold Resistance Buff   +1 Clothes / accessories   Low Luster (High = negative)   Stealth Ability Buff   +1 (−1) Clothes / accessories   Beautiful Pattern (Messy = negative)   CHA Buff   +1 (−1) Accessories   High Friction (Low = negative)   Knockdown Resistance Buff   +1% (−1%) Shirts / hats   Soft Surface · High Elasticity · Firm   Crafting · Gatherin

Attribute   Triggers on   Effect Vital Strike   critical hit (100%)   target Bleeding −6 Life/s for 10 s Seeing Red   critical hit (50%)   target Bleeding −4/s for 10 s Sadism   critical hit (100%)   you recover +6 Life/s for 10 s Budding Sadism   critical hit (50%)   you recover +4 Life/s for 10 s Throw Dirt   successful roll (50%)   enemy Distracted, accuracy −40% for 8 s Throw Dirt (minor)   successful roll (20%)   enemy accuracy −20% for 8 s Gathering Mania   successful gather/butcher (50%)   Invigorated, Energy +3/s for 10 s Extra Extra   gathering   10% chance of one extra item (the bonus piece gets attributes like the main piece) Secrets of Gathering   gathering (the tool you hold)   ×2 (+100%) chance of getting yellow, gray and green latent attributes · no effect when crafting Meticulous Gatherer   gathering   +5% Flawless gathering chance Pain Averse   roll / parry   roll and parry last 50% longer More Space   workbench   1 more unattended job Shorter Duration   workbench   −5% unattended crafting time Bleeding on animals really lowers their Life, and an animal that bleeds out leaves a carcass as usual · status icons appear on both players and animals What counts is every item you are wearing + the tool you gather with (duplicates use the highest level) · items at zero durability do not count

Attributes that give stats — every weather resistance, Defense Buff, Attack Buff, accuracy, critical, Durability Buff, crafting/gathering skills, base stats, stealth, Storage Capacity and so on — can come two ways on the same item: From the item's design — many grow with the item's level, e.g. Winter Fur Gloves carry Cold Resistance Buff = 1 + level × 0.05 (Lv60 = 4) · fractions round half up (3.95 → 4), except Storage Capacity, which rounds down Latent attributes picked up while gathering/crafting The level that really counts = design + latent (up to that attribute's maximum level) · the item info screen shows the total · the success label after crafting/gathering shows «Lv design → Lv total» Example (1 resistance point = −3% fatigue of that kind)   Cold Resistance   Cold fatigue Winter Fur Gloves Lv60, no latent   4   −12% Same gloves + latent Cold Resistance Buff 2   6   −18% Full 5-piece winter set Lv60, no latent   24   −72% Material/structure attributes (Strong, High Density and the like that recipes check) work as before: the latent value replaces the design value · recipe requirements do not change When crafting, only the latent value carries over; the result then adds its own design value Storage Capacity (from the bag-pocket modification or latent): level = extra bag slots (Storage) An item at zero durability — none of its attributes work (resistance, immunity, capacity, buffs) until repaired · the stats window updates as soon as it breaks or is repaired Food attrib

[!tip] Green attributes are very rare (0.1–0.3% per piece) — hold a high-level tool with «Secrets of Gathering» (×2) and butcher big animals (×2) to see them more often · a high Unstable Index raises the level of a source's fixed attribute, not the green chance [!tip] Several pieces in the main slot average the attribute level (rounded down) — fill every slot with pieces that share the attribute · for green attributes a single piece is enough [!tip] Long crafting chains no longer make attributes disappear — but some product types don't accept some attributes, so check the table above to see what each attribute is used for

sec.h: Not on the server yet: hazards these attributes block
sec.x: Some gear has «Lava Damage Prevention», «Spark Immunity» or «T-Rex Roar Prevention» — wearing it shows the status icon, but the server has no damaging lava, sparks or roars yet, so there is no visible effect. «Volcanic Storm Prevention», on the other hand, now works fully — see Volcanic Storm

d: Learn the seed's skill, build a plot, sow, water it fully, fertilize for more harvest — when it matures the crop survives or withers depending on water and the island's climate

sec.x: Grow your own plants on plots you build. Crops grow in real time, even while you are offline. When the growing time is up, the crop either succeeds (ready to harvest) or withers — water it fully and pick crops that suit the island's climate to keep it alive. Harvesting gives the produce (food, flowers, fiber and more) plus seeds back. Planting a seed

Build a Small Field / Large Field or a Flower Bed and plant one seed per plot You can only plant seeds whose skill you have learned (Corn and Apple are available from the start) · trees and big plants need a large 2×2 plot Give Water fully = high survival chance · Give Fertilizer = bigger harvest — neither one makes the crop grow faster Place a Sprinkler to water many plots at once (multipurpose models also spread liquid fertilizer) Use Rapid Growth to pay Warp Gems and finish a crop instantly Harvesting gives Farming skill exp and levels up that seed's Farming Encyclopedia entry, which unlocks specializations

Build a plot (see Building). Plots you can plant in: Plot   Size (tiles)   Large seeds Small Field · Small Gray Field   1×1   No Large Field · Large Gray Field   2×2   Yes Small Flower Bed (Wood / Stone / Horn)   1×1   No Wide Flower Bed (Wood / Stone / Horn)   2×2   Yes Walk up to the plot, choose Plant Seed  and pick a seed from your bag While it grows, use Give Water  (with Water or Hot Spring Water — Sea Water does not work · fresh water in a container you filled works too, and the plot takes only what it still lacks) and Give Fertilizer  (any item with the Compost property — see Fertilizer and yield) When it shows Available to Harvest, tap the plot — there is a harvest button named after the crop (done bare-handed, like the gathering menu); press it and wait for the progress bar to fill to get the produce · Remove Crop  still works and gives the same produce The plot's label shows the crop's name (for example Wheat), not the raw seed code [!warn] Removing a crop before it is ripe gives the seed back (same level) but no produce and no exp. Fertilizing a plot

Every character gets the Corn and Apple skills for free from the start Every other seed needs its own skill in the Farming category first (unlocked at category level 10–60) — see the list in Skill list Not learned yet = the game says «… skill is required» with a button to view the skill · the seed is kept Large seeds (marked «» in the growing-time table) can't go on a 1×1 plot — the seed is kept · a large crop already planted on a small plot keeps growing and can be harvested normally 7 special seeds (Carnation · Watermelon · Cherry · Donarium Cherry Sapling · Peepkin · Spider Web Tree · Cacao Tree) have no skill to unlock — plant them as soon as you get them Event seeds can only be planted during their event: Carnation · White Rose (1–31 May) · Jasmine (1–31 Aug) — outside it the game says it can't be planted · White Rose and Jasmine still need their normal skill

During the Halloween event (20 Oct – 10 Nov) every check-in gives 3 Peepkin Seeds and 1 Spider Web Tree Seed (the weekly Halloween ladder adds more) — they can only be planted during this window, on a large 2×2 plot, with no skill needed Seed   Grows in   Produce Peepkin Seed   1 hour   Peepkin Spider Web Tree Seed   21 hours   Spider Web · Spider · Branch You can harvest after the event has ended and keep using the produce (event seeds can't be planted again until next year)

Growing times follow the original game's crop data — the 11 crops in the community sheet (Corn, Potato, Wheat, Sugar Cane, Rice, Tea Tree, Coffee, Grape, Fig, Banana, Watermelon) use the sheet values (at least 1 minute, no upper cap). Watering, fertilizing, sprinklers and rain do not make crops grow faster — the only ways to shorten it are the «Growth Time» specialization (−10%) and Rapid Growth. Crops planted before this system keep their old time. When the growing time is up, the game decides once whether the crop succeeds or withers (logging out and back in gives the same result). Crops planted before this system always succeed. survival chance = seed toughness × climate × water + Farming Ability bonus   (max 100%) Seed toughness — 55–100% depending on the crop (Corn 90% · Banana 82% · Mango/Orange 70% · Apple 100%) Water — based on the water in the plot when the time is up: full = full value · none at all = half · in between = proportional · 1 water item = 1 unit · crops need 1–40 units (Apple needs none · Corn 1 · Potato 2 · Wheat 3) · you can't water a full plot (no water is wasted) · rain waters plots too (Weather) Climate — see the Climate Suitability line on the plot's info: Excellent ×1.05 · Good ×0.9 · Normal ×0.7 · Bad ×0.5 (fixed when you plant) Farming Ability of whoever planted it (value at sowing) — each point adds 1% × toughness, up to 25 points · the Cultivation I–V skills give 4 points each · food and gear that raise Farming Ability count too Fertilizer has no effect on survival · once the time is up you can no longer water or fertilize (the game says the crop is fully grown) Example, Corn (toughness 90%): Climate   Fully watered   Never watered   Fully watered + Cultivation I–V Excellent   94.5%   47.3%   100% Good   81%   40.5%   99% Normal   63%   31.5%   81% Bad   45%   22.5%   63% (Corn is a sheet crop, so it never goes below «Normal» — the «Bad» row applies to crops outside the sheet with the sam

Climates sit in a row Snowfield – Tundra – Temperate – Grassland – Tropical – Desert – Volcano. An island matching the crop's favorite = Excellent · 1 step away = Good · 2 steps = Normal · 3 or more = Bad. Swamp islands count as Temperate · Savanna islands and the tamed islands count as Grassland. The 11 crops in the sheet (Corn, Potato, Wheat, Sugar Cane, Rice, Tea Tree, Coffee, Grape, Fig, Banana, Watermelon) follow the sheet's rule: the favorite island = Excellent · the sheet's worst island = Bad (Rice, Banana, Coffee — Tundra · Tea Tree — Tropical) · other islands are counted by distance from the favorite but never below Normal Likes   Crops Grassland   Corn · Onion · Flax · Bean · Sunflower · Mr. Lincoln Rose · Damask Rose · Lavender · Red Poppy · Ume Tree · Oleander · Maple Tree · Ginkgo Tree · Watermelon (also likes Temperate) Temperate   Potato · Pumpkin · Wheat · Barley · Tomato · Mushroom · Cosmos · White Rose · Wild Rose · Carnation · Cherry · Donarium Cherry · Watermelon · Grape · Fig · Persimmon Tree · Sugar Cane Tropical   Jasmine · Oxalis · Rice · Tropical Flax · Chili Pepper · Bell Pepper · Taro · Mango · Orange · Banana · Coffee · Cacao Tree Tundra   Cotton · Tea Tree · Peepkin · Spider Web Tree Desert   Purple Tulip · Desert Agave Every island (always Excellent)   Apple Example on a tamed island (Grassland): grassland crops = Excellent · temperate/tropical crops = Good · tundra/desert crops = Normal.

Fertilize until Soil Fertility is 100% = the harvest rises to the crop's «fully fertilized» amount in its table · half = halfway between «none» and «full» · extra fertilizer adds nothing · the fraction is a chance for one more piece Crops outside the 11 sheet crops use the old rule: fully fertilized ×1.6 · half ×1.3 (for example fully fertilized Corn used to give 1.6× the base) Fertilizer counts by the amount of each piece (the same number the fertilizer window shows) · crops need 10–200 depending on the type (Corn 10 · Potato 30 · Wheat 40) · the fertilize option disappears once it is full The Nutritious attribute on a fertilizer adds +12.5% amount per level … Harvesting Buff attributes (Vegetable · Fruit · Grain · Flower · Leaf · Wood · Fiber) add +10% (level 1) up to +50% (level 11) harvest for crops of that type · with several pieces, the strongest one counts Making yield-boosting fertilizer yourself — the «Fermented Fruit Growth Fertilizer» recipe gives only one buff, chosen by the additive: Charcoal → Vegetable · Seashell or Horseshoe Crab Shell → Fruit · Bone → Grain · the «Fermented Leaf/Stalk Growth Fertilizer» recipe: seeds (grain seeds too) → Fiber · fish → Wood · fruit → Leaf · grain → Flower (fertilizer made before the update keeps buffing every type) Fertilizer (items with the Compost property)   Amount per piece, Lv1 → Lv60 Grass Fertilizer   1.5 → 90 (1.5 × level) Primitive Fertilizer   6.6 → 42 Quality Fertilizer · Liquid Fertilizer   11 → 70 Fruit Fertilizer

Touch a sprinkler and choose Give Water — every plot in its spray area that is still growing gets water by model, with no water taken from your bag. A sprinkler has limited uses that recharge one at a time (the remaining uses are on its info page · when it's out, the game tells you how many minutes until the next charge). A crop that is still growing has a Rapid Growth button — pay Warp Gems and it finishes instantly (your character's real Warp Gems are spent, the same number the window shows). The price drops as the remaining time goes down. Success or withering is decided right away with the same chance (Rapid Growth does not help it survive). Anyone allowed to use the plot can press it (and pays themselves). Each seed type has its own encyclopedia level (max 20). The encyclopedia page shows the real growing time, water and fertilizer of the 11 sheet crops (you see them after returning to the title screen or logging in again). Each harvest gives +20 exp, and the number of harvests needed depends on the crop (fast crops need more harvests than trees). Exp you already had is kept and your level is recalculated with these thresholds (nobody loses a level). Whoever built a plot can always do everything with it · others can sow, water, fertilize, use Rapid Growth or uproot/harvest only when: Where the plot is   What others need On someone's Domain   all 3 permissions Use + Give + Take from the Domain owner (friends use the Friends tab), or that plot's own per-item permission Outside any Domain   a per-item permission the plot owner opened for that plot — otherwise only the plot owner can use it No permission = the plot's buttons are greyed out and nothing is taken from your bag · a sprinkler on someone else's Domain needs the «Use» permission · encyclopedia exp only goes to whoever planted the crop — harvesting a friend's plot gives the produce but no encyclopedia exp · see Domain for setting permissions · boxes and workbenches on someone else's Domain use a different set of permissions, see Boxes, workbenches and pens on someone else's Domain

[!tip] Fill the water before the crop matures — the water in the plot at that moment is what decides survival. Plot water never drains by itself, so one full watering is enough, and rain can do it for you. [!tip] On a tamed island (Grassland), Corn, Onion, Flax and Bean get an «Excellent» climate. To grow tundra or desert crops with better survival, learn Cultivation I–V first. [!tip] Harvested vegetables, fruit and mushrooms spoil within 3 days, while grains (corn, rice, wheat, beans, barley) and apples don't — see Preserving food. [!tip] Event seeds (Carnation, White Rose, Jasmine, Peepkin, Spider Web Tree) can only be planted during their event; outside it the game tells you the seed can't be planted.

sec.h: Some produce is still a generic item
sec.x: For 21 crops the original game's specific produce is unknown, so they currently give a generic item instead, e.g. ornamental flowers → Flower · Maple Tree/Ginkgo Tree → Leaf · Banana Tree, Mango, Orange → Tropical Fruit · Fig Tree → Normal Fruit. Some of them (e.g. Banana, Fig, Lavender, Purple Tulip) carry a plant name tag, so recipes asking for that plant still accept them. This may change once more data is found.

sec.h: Boxes that give items in rounds
sec.x: Lost Package · Wooden Clothes Box · Wooden Seed Box (decorations on islands, not structures) give at most 5 items per box and grow back with a new roll — see Gathering Items from traps (including the animal traps that exist on the server) are named after the species and can get latent attributes just like butchering — see Names that show where an item came from

d: Items come in categories — weapons/tools · clothing · materials · food/medicine · seeds — levels, where they come from, locking and discarding

Touch an item → Item Info to see its level, Durability and attributes Lock items you don't want to lose — locked or equipped items can't be discarded and can't be listed on the market Weapons, tools, clothing and accessories wear out with use — they can be repaired (Equipment and repair) Your bag holds 200 items · you can discard items onto the ground as a bundle (10 T-Stones per discard — Discarding items)

d: 3 swappable equipment sets + Decorative Gear (costumes) · weapons/gear wear out with use · repair with repair kits (4 random results) or T-Stones (always flawless) · dyeing and bleaching

sec.x: Weapons, tools, clothing and accessories are equipped to use their values (Character stats) · they wear out with use · at 0 Durability they give nothing until you repair them

Slot   What goes in Main hand / off hand   One-handed weapons, tools · two-handed items take both slots Head   Hats · hooded outfits take head and body Body   Tops/outfits Gloves · shoes · bag   By type Accessory   Necklaces, rings and so on Equipping something that clashes with a slot takes the old item off automatically · there is no minimum level to equip — an item's values come from that item's level 3 equipment sets — swap instantly (e.g. a fighting set / gathering set / building set) · all sets are unlocked Decorative Gear (costumes) — some fashion items always go into a separate set (they change your look only — they don't replace your fighting gear and give no stats) — see Decorative Gear Items in any set (even a spare one) can't be discarded or put in a box until you take them off

sec.h: Other item stats apply while worn
sec.x: Besides attack/defense, the other stats written on an item (Max Health, evasion, weather resistance, speed, bag capacity and so on) and the item's attributes really take effect, but only for items worn in the set you are using — the effect of each stat is listed in Clothing and accessories

Fashion items that are Decorative Gear (many have «(Decorative)» in the name) go into the head and body slots of the Decorative Gear set, which is separate from your 3 fighting sets — your character really changes look, on your own screen and for the people around you A costume covers your armor only in the slot it occupies — a slot with no costume still shows the armor of the set you're using (wear just a costume hat and your body still shows your armor) A hooded costume takes the head and body slots together Stats, buffs and item stats come only from the fighting set you're using — a costume adds or removes nothing Take the costume off and the armor in that slot shows again · usable on every island 6 costumes come with an outfit motion — the item details name the motion, and while you wear the costume it is listed as a motion that comes from the outfit (every motion is still usable by everyone, as before)

New items have 100 Durability (a flawless craft gets 110 · materials gathered, butchered or harvested flawlessly stay at 100) · they wear when: Item   Wears when The weapon you hold   You land a hit — by half the damage dealt Every gear piece you wear   You get hit — by the damage taken Gathering tools   Each successful gather (a failure wears half as much) Hammers/saws when building   Each build or modification, 4 at a time Taming tools   Every capture attempt Per use ≈ 0.35 × (1% of max Durability + damage × 0.001), at least 0.2% of max Durability — e.g. a 100-Durability sword hitting for 100 damage (half counted = 50) loses ≈ 0.37 per hit (about 270 hits) At 0 Durability a weapon gives no attack, gear gives no defense and its other stats stop working · the item doesn't vanish, it can be repaired The «durability» attribute on materials raises max Durability (Item attributes)

Touch the item in your bag → Repair (no workbench needed) · 3-second bar · only weapons/tools, clothing and accessories can be repaired · items at full Durability can't be repaired Required repair power = item level² ÷ 100 (rounded down · minimum 5) Item level   1–24   30   40   50   60 Required repair power   5   9   16   25   36 Energy used = required repair power × 0.8

Pick repair kits of the matching type whose total power ≥ the requirement — the kits are used up Repair kit   Repair power   Repairs Tool Repair Kit — Budget / Standard / Quality   30 / 90 / 150   Weapons, tools Clothing Repair Kit — Budget / Standard / Quality   30 / 90 / 150   Clothing, accessories You can craft repair kits yourself (Weapons and tools) There are 4 random results — the more power you put in above the requirement (up to 2×) and the more crafting skill you have (Weapon/Tool or Tailoring), the better Power supplied ÷ required   Flawless   Success   Failure   Big failure 1× · no skill   8%   57%   23%   12% 2× · no skill   20%   67%   6%   7% 2× · full skill bonus   32%   60%   5%   3% Result   Durability after repair Flawless   Full · max Durability unchanged Success   Full · max Durability −3% Failure   Full · max Durability −8% Big failure   Full · max Durability −18% Max Durability can drop to 2 at the lowest — below that the game won't let you repair it any more Crafting skill bonus = skill tiers learned in the category ÷ 2 (1–8)

Choose no kits → pay T-Stones equal to the required repair power (the number on the button — repairing an item costs T-Stones, not Warp Gems) · the result is always flawless (max Durability unchanged) — a level 60 item costs 36 T-Stones per repair [!tip] T-Stones are cheaper and never cost max Durability — keep repair kits for when you're out of T-Stones · repairing structures uses different rules (building repair kits, or Repair Now with Warp Gems)

At a Dye Workbench: pick an item + a color channel (each item has 1–3 dyeable channels) + a dye → 5-second bar → that channel shifts 50% toward the dye's color (halfway between the old color and the dye) · dye again to get even closer to the dye's color Bleaching (with a decolorizer) returns the channel to the item's original color · each use consumes 1 dye · dyes and decolorizers are made at the same workbench (Food, drinks and medicine)

sec.x: Clothing gives defense and stats (see Character stats) · equipping, removing and repairing is on Equipment and repair Early career outfits are made at a Workbench, the advanced Lv60 ones are sewn at a Tailoring Workbench · most fashion items are sold in the Shop — fashion packs (paid in Durango Coins) or random Express Cargo boxes (Fashion / Decorative Gear, 100 Warp Gems per box) · profession name tags come in 100-Durango-Coin packs · a few can be bought with Loyalty points at the Loyalty Shop [!tip] The «Where from» column in the tables lists the easiest way first — «Craft (hands)» = anywhere, no workbench · a name in brackets = the workbench you must stand next to · Shop prices are in Durango Coins / Warp Gems / Loyalty as written · «Not obtainable yet» = there is no way to get that item on this server right now (its level shows «—»)

sec.x: Food is your character's main source of Energy. Besides energy, some foods restore health, give stat buffs, help against heat or cold, or boost the exp you earn when they taste good — but you can't binge-eat, because a hidden "satiety" meter holds you back. Eating

Eat food from your bag → get its full energy right away, plus the food's other effects Drink Water at a river, lake or sea shore without needing a bottle or item Eat tasty food to get the Delicious status (more exp) and foods that give the Enhanced Ability buff Cook before eating to avoid Stomach Pain from raw food (see Cooking)

Open your bag, pick a food and choose Eat (drinks: Drink) — your character plays an eating animation, then the effect applies Stand next to water and choose Drink Water — takes 5 seconds and gives +5 energy and the Water status, same as drinking a bottle of water, without using an item · the effect applies when the bar completes — starting something else, or walking more than 1 tile from where you started, during the bar cancels that drink (one at a time) · you can also drink from a container you filled with water (choose the container in the «Eat» menu — one unit at a time, the container stays) — see Water containers If you eat a different buff food while a food buff is still active, the game asks "Previous food's effect will disappear. Continue?" — confirm and the new buff replaces the old one

There is no satiety bar on screen, but the server tracks it in the background: Every food has its own satiety value, added when you eat it Satiety caps at 100 and digests steadily, from 100 down to empty in 30 minutes While you are below 100 you can always eat, even if that bite takes you over 100 Once you reach 100 you get the Full status and can't eat; the game tells you roughly how many seconds/minutes to wait Dying or levelling up removes Full immediately Drink Water from a water source does not count toward satiety Food   Satiety per piece   Pieces until Full (from empty)   Steady rate (pieces/hour) Water   5   20   40 Apple · Minnow · Egg · Raspberry   10   10   20 Meat Kebab   12   9   16.7 Bread · Meat-Stuffed Bread · Sashimi · Root   15   7   13.3 Meat   20   5   10 Tenderloin Steak   50   2   4 Fat   120   1   1.7

With Luxurious Ambiance from a house (Buffs) your satiety drops 0.5% slower per total mood level of the house (at most 90% slower) Total mood level   Satiety drops slower by   Full to empty No mood   —   30 minutes 15   7.5%   about 32 minutes 40   20%   37.5 minutes This makes you stay full longer and eat less often — the in-game description says it shortens satiety, but this server follows the decision made for it When the buff ends or changes, satiety goes back to the normal rate from that moment (the time before is not recalculated)

All of a food's taste values (sweet, salty, savory, oily, spicy, bitter, sour) add up to one score: Taste score   Status   Effect (5 minutes) 3 or more   Delicious   Character exp from actions ×1.03 −3 or less   Horrible   More fatigue In between   —   Nothing Properties on a food item change its taste — anything with the Raw property tastes much worse (raw meat = Horrible + Stomach Pain), but cooking removes Raw, so the same meat becomes Delicious. Eating raw food also cancels Delicious.

Effect   Details Enhanced Ability   Stat buff (e.g. Strength, Will, Agility, Max Energy) for 5–30 minutes depending on the food · one set at a time · eating the same food again refreshes it · lost on death Percentage recovery   Some foods restore health/energy as a share of your maximum Hot Food / Cold Food   Food with the Hot property helps against cold (but you feel heat more in hot places) · Cold is the reverse Stomach Pain   From food with the Raw property, or spoiled food Cooldown   Potent Health Recovery Medicine (and a few event items) gives Overexerted for 5 minutes, during which you can't take another of the same kind Level limit   Booster Jelly Piece and Booster Jelly can only be eaten at levels 20–55 · they give instant exp of about 3.4% and 34% of the exp needed for your current level Ability/stat buffs from spices and toppings   seasoned grilled meat, Pizza, Stuffed Bread, Garnished Fried Noodles, Cream Cake — see Spices and toppings

Some medicines and foods last longer: Item   Effect lasts Anti-Bleeding Agent · Painkiller Root   20 minutes (was 5) Rash Preventative   30 minutes (was 20) Tetanus Preventative   45 minutes Poison Gas Preventative   60 minutes Bug Poison Preventative · Lizard Poison Preventative · Internal Bleeding Preventative · Hemorrhagic Poison Preventative   20 minutes Survival Food   10 minutes (was 5) The 7 preventatives above now really give their protective status when eaten, at the item's level (before, some gave nothing at all) · the status disappears if you die

sec.h: Effects from a food's own attributes
sec.x: Some foods carry an attribute of their own; its level grows with the item's level (fractions round half up) and it takes effect when eaten: Food   Own attribute   When eaten Mushroom   Poisonous to Humans level 1 (Lv1–9) · 2 (Lv10–29) · 3 (Lv30–49) · 4 (Lv50–69) · 5 (Lv70)   Eaten raw — including dried, smoked, pickled or canned — gives Poisoned for 1 minute: Health −(0.5 + 0.5 × level)/second = −60 to −180 in total · cooking it with fire/water/oil removes the poison and gives Hot Food instead Freshwater Eel   Stamina Food level 1–5 (same level bands as the mushroom)   Raw = Stomach Pain · cooked (skewer, boil, steam, grill, fry …) = Stamina Recovery Speed Buff at the same level for 5 minutes (instead of Hot Food) · dried/smoked/pickled = no effect Ice · Shaved Ice   Cold = item level   Cold Food at the item's level, up to 5 · Ice 5 minutes · Shaved Ice 20 minutes Barley Drink   Fatigue Debuff = item level   Quenching Drink for 5 minutes: Fatigue −0.18 × level per minute (Lv60 ≈ −54 over the 5 minutes) Dried Persimmon   Max Health, Max Energy Buff = item level   Surging Sweetness for 5 minutes: Max Health +2 × level · Max Energy +0.5 × level The item info screen shows the effect level you really get when eating (never above the status's maximum) — e.g. Lv10 Ice shows Cold Food level 5 Stat effects from food statuses (e.g. Strange Eats, Will +3) now count on your character sheet Levelling up right after eating a raw mushroom clears the poison at once Eating together

Gathering, crafting and other work cost energy. If you have less energy than an action needs, the game warns you first and lets you choose to eat first or carry on — for the energy and fatigue gauges see Survival.

[!tip] Grill meat with the Skewer recipe before eating — same energy, but no Stomach Pain and you get Delicious (exp ×1.03). [!tip] High-satiety foods (Fat, steak) fill you up fast. If you need lots of energy, pick foods with high energy but low satiety, such as Apple. [!tip] You can only have one Enhanced Ability buff at a time — don't accidentally eat a different buff food over the one you want.
The "water" value of food has no effect yet (the game has no water gauge) The Phenomenal Flavor and Disgusting statuses never happen, because the game data has no thresholds for them

d: Cook ingredients at a bonfire or kitchen — removes rawness and adds heat/cold, flavor and special properties per recipe

sec.x: Recipes in the Cooking category improve the same ingredient — grilled meat is still meat, but it is no longer Raw and gains new properties depending on how it was cooked, such as Hot (helps against cold) or Boost Umami. New dishes (bread, cheese, sausage, etc.) are made through normal crafting, see Crafting. Kitchen and bonfires

Grill, roast, simmer, steam, deep-fry, stir-fry, boil, brew tea, make pills and iced drinks — every recipe removes the Raw property (no more Stomach Pain) Preserve food (smoking, drying, pickling, canning) — same category, see Preserving food Unlock new recipes with Cooking skills (see Skills)

Go to a station with a Cooking Fire (bonfire, kitchen, etc.), or a Drying Rack / Medical Lab depending on the recipe, and choose Craft Pick a recipe in the Cooking category, put an edible ingredient in the main slot and hold the tool the recipe needs (Stick, Stone Plate, Pot, Frying Pan, Metal Grate, Mortar, Container, Cutting Board) Wait for the timer bar; you get the same ingredient back, cooked Each cooking uses 1 of that item's processing chances (3 per item) — see Preserving food The bonfire must be lit — you cannot grill/craft at a bonfire that has gone out (the game says so in a Thai-only message: «กองไฟดับอยู่ — จุดไฟก่อน», "the bonfire is out — light it first") · player-placed bonfires die out by themselves when nobody uses them (Bonfires dying out and disappearing)

Each station's Cooking Fire/Countertop has a level — a recipe appears once the level reaches what the recipe needs. A station's level = the level of that building, but no higher than the cap in this table. Station   Cooking Fire   Other Bonfire   19   — Large Bonfire · Cooking Bonfire · Camping Grill   60   — Stove   59   Countertop 59 Kitchen · Civilized Island Kitchen · Ash Wood Table   60   Countertop 60 Lava Kitchen   60   Countertop 60 · Lava Kitchen 60 Small Drying Rack (2 kinds)   —   Drying Rack 39 or 60 Large Drying Rack   —   Drying Rack 60 Medical Lab   —   Medical Lab 60 A Small Drying Rack can't tan leather — tanning recipes, some leather drying and the special preserving recipes need a Drying Rack of level 40, but the small rack tops out at 39 → use a Large Drying Rack · the small rack handles the basic drying recipes (6 recipes at Drying Rack 15)

The Oven (the building that is a basic cooking stove in the original game) and the camp Oven can now cook — the Oven's Cooking Fire level is 39 (38 in camps), so it makes recipes up to Fire 39 (68 of the 94 recipes that use a Cooking Fire); Fire 40+ recipes still need a kitchen or a big bonfire · it still smelts ore and makes nails as before · Ovens built before the update get the new level by themselves when the island loads

"Hot N" = the Hot property at level N → eating it gives the Hot Food status · the level follows the fire tier the recipe uses (fire 1 → 1 · fire 15 → 2 · fire 40+ → 3) · "Unlock" = the Cooking category level at which the recipe's skill can be learned. Property   Effect Hot   Eating it gives Hot Food — more resistant to cold (but you feel heat more in hot places); higher levels resist more Cold   Eating it gives Cold Food — more resistant to heat (but colder in cold places) Boost Umami   Savory taste +1 and energy +3 per level Deep Fried / Stir-fry   More savory and oily taste, but removes that food's max-energy buff Recovery Medicine   Health restored by the food ×1.5 / ×1.8 / ×2.1 (level 1/2/3) Attack Buff / Defense Buff   Attack +3.3 / defense +2.3 per level while the food buff lasts Softness   No effect yet (the game data itself says so) Cooking ingredients that have an effect of their own: a Mushroom loses its poison when cooked (Hot Food instead) · a Freshwater Eel gives the Stamina Recovery Speed Buff instead of Hot Food once cooked — see Eating and drinking

The 3 seasoned grill recipes (Seasoned Stone Plate BBQ · Spicy Roast · Seasoned Grillade) take a spice in the seasoning slot, and the food gets stat buffs by spice +2 per stat (Flawless +4 · an ordinary failed craft 0) instead of the old «Boost Umami 1» Spice   Stats Honey · Sugar   Charisma · Will · Perception Chili Pepper   Strength · Intelligence · Endurance Bell Pepper   Strength · Dexterity · Perception Salt   Strength · Perception Herb   Strength · Agility · Will The seasoned drying, smoking and salting recipes still give «Boost Umami 1» whatever spice you put in.

Put an ingredient in the topping slot of Pizza · Stuffed Bread · Garnished Fried Noodles · Cream Cake and eating it gives a +4 ability buff by ingredient (Flawless +6 · an ordinary failed craft still +4): Topping   Ability Meat   Mining Cheese   Slaughter Aged Cheese   Slaughter + Plant Gathering Onion   Plant Gathering Tomato   Cooking Pumpkin   Farming Bell Pepper   Weapon Crafting Chili Pepper   Metal Processing Potato   Building Bean   Furniture Crafting Grape   Sewing Banana   Handicraft Fig   Tailoring Fish, mushrooms, insects, eggs and anything else give no ability · seeds don't count as toppings (only the produce)

Stuffed Bread — stats by filling 46 at Lv60 (meat = Strength · vegetable = Dexterity · fruit = Charisma · fish = Agility) · the old Will 30 is gone Garnished Fried Noodles — the dish's Intelligence + the sauce's stats + the topping's stats (meat = Strength · vegetable = Dexterity · fruit = Charisma · fish = Agility · 46 at Lv60) Cream Cake — Charisma 46 at Lv60 (use fruit as the topping) Recipes that make several items at once (Cake ×4 · Noodles ×2 · Pizza ×4) give every piece the buff

Premium Sausage has more energy (277 at Lv58 · was 241), Satiety 15 and Perception 40 instead of Strength · cooking it further changes the energy by method (at Lv58 — other levels scale in proportion): Method   Energy Deep-fry   320 Stir-fry   297 Boil   280 (Satiety 7) Steam   277 Stone Plate BBQ   283 Smoke   292 · the Premium Sausage's buffs are lost (other foods keep their buffs when smoked) Combining ingredients

[!tip] A great success while cooking gives +1 level to the Hot/Cold property (e.g. Skewer gives Hot 2). [!tip] Fire 40+ recipes don't work on a plain Bonfire (cap 19) — use a Large Bonfire or a kitchen built from high-enough-level materials. [!tip] Some recipes, such as pills and herbal tea, need a Dried ingredient — dry, smoke or pickle it first, then make the medicine.

sec.h: Cooked food color · garnish · detox soup
sec.x: Cooked food doesn't change color yet (in the original, grilling darkens it) Steamed Dish with Garnish doesn't apply effects from the garnish yet Boiled Ingredients with medicinal ingredients doesn't remove poison yet

d: Fresh food fully spoils in 3 days — smoke, dry, pickle or can it to make it last longer · each item can be processed 3 times

sec.x: Meat, fish, vegetables and fruit slowly spoil in real time. Preservation recipes make food last longer, at the cost of losing the ingredient's status/buff effects. On top of that, every item has limited processing chances — it can be cooked or preserved at most 3 times. Smoked food
Smoke, dry, pickle and can fresh food so it keeps longer Draw sea water to make Salt for pickling List food on the market without worrying about spoilage (listed items stop spoiling)

All of them are in the Cooking category, Preservation group · put an edible item in the main slot. Recipe   Needs   Extra ingredients   Result   Max durability   Unlock Smoked Ingredients   Cooking Fire 1   —   Dried · Smoked   ×1.65   10 Smoked Spicy Food   Cooking Fire 15   Spice   Dried · Smoked · Boost Umami   ×1.65   25 Dried Food   Drying Rack 15   —   Dried · Boost Retention 1   ×1.5   20 Dry Spiced Food   Drying Rack 15   Spice   + Boost Umami   ×1.5   35 Pickled Ingredients   Drying Rack 15   Salt   Dried · Boost Retention 1   ×1.5   30 Pickled & Spicy   Drying Rack 40   Salt · Spice   + Boost Umami   ×1.5   45 Improvised Canned Food   Workbench 40   Container · Water · Glue   Boost Retention 1   ×1.5   50 Standard Canned Food   Workbench 60   Container · Oil · Glue   Boost Retention 2   ×2   60

The Raw property is removed by every recipe · Freshness is removed by smoking, drying and pickling Ingredient properties that give statuses or buffs are stripped, e.g. Hot, Cold, Recovery Medicine, Attack Buff, Defense Buff and other medicine/buff effects Taste and energy properties (e.g. Boost Umami, Boost Sweetness, Deep Fried) are kept Harmful properties such as Poisonous to Humans are not removed (preserving doesn't make food safe) — dried, smoked, pickled or canned mushrooms still poison you for 1 minute, like raw ones (Eating and drinking) The food type's own built-in effects (e.g. Bread's max-energy buff) stay, since it is still the same item Sausage, Premium Sausage and Witch Sausage also don't inherit status/buff properties from the meat used Smoked Premium Sausage also loses its Perception buff and its energy becomes 292 (at Lv58) — Premium Sausage only; other foods keep their design buffs when smoked (Premium Sausage)

Spoils   Doesn't spoil Meat, intestine, fish, eggs, fruit, vegetables, mushrooms, berries (47 kinds), including the same items after cooking or preserving, e.g. grilled meat, pickled meat   New dishes (bread, soup, steak, sausage, cheese, sashimi, etc.) · drinks, milk, water, sea water · Apple · grains · flowers, leaves, roots, herbs · insects · seeds · nuts

Fresh food starts at Durability 100 and drops steadily to 0 in 3 days (33.3 per day). The speed is the same for every item, so preserved food with a higher max durability lasts longer. State   Max durability   Fully spoiled after Fresh   100   3 days Dried · Pickled · Improvised Canned   150   4.5 days Smoked   165   about 5 days Standard Canned   200   6 days Durability counts down on screen by itself Food spoils everywhere — bag, warehouse, boxes, pet bags, mail, entrust tables — except items listed on the market (paused, then resumes when bought or withdrawn) Items the market sends back by mail (listing expired/cancelled) resume spoiling from the moment they leave the market — sitting in the mailbox does not stop it Preserving partly spoiled food = the remaining durability + the extra (e.g. 50/100 → dried becomes 100/150)

The item does not disappear and you can still eat it — energy, taste and satiety work as normal But eating it gives Stomach Pain, and the food's status/buff effects don't work The game shows it as Destroyed (sorted to the end of the bag) and it can't go into crafting slots · the in-game text says to Repair it, but food can't be repaired

Stand by the sea with a container (bottle, flask, bucket, pot and so on) and choose Draw Water → the container fills with Sea Water (a river or lake gives ordinary Water · standing exactly between sea and fresh water gives fresh water · drawing sea water into a container that holds fresh water pours the old water out) — see Water containers Make Salt from 3 units of Sea Water at Cooking Fire 15 (pick a container holding sea water for the ingredient slot — one unit per pick, and the container is kept) (unlocked by the Salt, Sugar skill at Cooking level 25) Use the salt in Pickled Ingredients / Pickled & Spicy Sea Water can't be used to water crops (neither can a container full of it).

Each item can be processed 3 times. Recipes whose craft window shows Processing Chance Consumed 1 (all cooking/preservation recipes and most other processing recipes) use 1 chance from the item in the main slot. At 0 the item can't be processed further — the server refuses and your ingredients are not taken (both for your own crafting and entrusted crafting) Dye recipes don't use processing chances Some foods made from an ingredient — Meat Dumpling, Aged Cheese, Boiled Meat — inherit the main ingredient's remaining chances minus 1 Old items that had been processed more than 3 times before this rule now have 0 left

[!tip] Preserve early — the fresher the food when you preserve it, the longer it lasts. Standard Canned Food lasts longest (6 days). [!tip] Preservation strips the ingredient's buffs — eat food with good buff properties fresh, and preserve plain meat for storage. [!tip] Plan each item's processing: grill once + preserve once still leaves 1 chance.
Some points are still awaiting a decision, e.g. whether apples and nuts should spoil, and whether grains/herbs should — the lists on this page may change.
The seasoned preserving recipes (drying, smoking, salting) always give Boost Umami 1, whatever spice you add · the seasoned grill recipes already give stat buffs by spice — see Spices.

d: Build houses, furniture, workbenches and boxes — pick a site, add materials, build, then maintain, repair, demolish or package them

sec.x: Player-built houses and a party yard Everything a player places on the ground — tents, houses, workbenches, bonfires, boxes, furniture — is a structure. You build it from a blueprint unlocked through skills (Skills) and fill it with materials from your bag.

Select a construction site → add materials → build (some structures then need extra time to finish) Let friends help with finalization, or pay Warp Gems for instant construction Use it: open boxes, craft at workbenches, light/put out fires, open/close gates, rest in tents, name it, write on signs Houses: modify parts, change textures, place wall decorations, extend floors, complete furniture sets Repair when Durability drops (Decay and repair) · demolish to get materials back · package it and place it elsewhere

Open Structure Building and pick a blueprint you have learned (unlearned blueprints cannot be built) Select Construction Site on the ground — you must stand within 4 tiles and it must not overlap another structure Touch the site and put materials into each slot (the item's tags must match the slot) — anyone can help put materials into a site · once everything is in, the slots fill right away (no need to close and reopen the window), and other players with the same site open see the new materials at once When all slots are full, press Build once — the build bar runs (its length depends on the structure's size, see Key numbers), and when it fills the structure appears, finishing at the same moment for everyone nearby · some blueprints need a hammer (or saw) in your bag; the tool wears each time a build succeeds If the blueprint has a finishing time, the structure stays translucent with scaffolding until the time is up, then it becomes usable If you walk away or start another action during the build bar, the build is cancelled — the materials stay in the site, no energy is used, and you can press Build again right away. A structure's level = the average level of the materials you used (within the blueprint's level range) · workbenches get workbench tags capped at this level and may inherit special properties from the main material (Item tags) [!tip] Always build on your own Domain — structures outside a Domain break within 1 day and vanish if nobody uses them. See Domain and Dec

Free ground not covered by another structure · discarded item bundles on the ground block building just like structures — pick the bundle up first, then build over it (Storage) Not allowed: in water · on top of trees/rocks/plants that are still standing (felled ones don't block) · tiles the game marks as unbuildable · on the tutorial island — the same rules as the colored frame when you pick a site Someone else's Domain: not allowed unless the owner grants the «Build» permission (Domain) Tamed Islands: you can only build and place things inside your own Domain — claim a Domain first (Domain) Furniture in houses follows the original game's rules: The house must be finished, and the piece must sit entirely inside the house frame — you can't straddle the line between inside and outside (Barracks have no walls, so they can be straddled) In multi-floor houses you can stack furniture on different floors (upper floor above lower-floor furniture) · a tall piece must not be taller than the floors left in the house, and every floor it covers must be free Tiles the game marks as no-place inside a building can't be used (for example some rows of a Sauna) Indoor-only items can't be placed outside · items that can't go indoors can't be placed over a house Newly built or newly placed Barracks, Saunas, Cabins and Shelters can hold furniture inside

Item   Value Distance you must stand within (select site/build/use/repair/demolish)   4 tiles Site selection time   2 + tiles covered (seconds) Energy for site selection   1 + 2 × tiles covered Energy to press Build   1 Build bar (after pressing Build)   2 + tiles covered (seconds) — 1 tile ≈ 3 s · 2×2 ≈ 6 s · 3×3 ≈ 11 s · 6×4 ≈ 26 s · dragging a house bigger makes the bar longer Demolish bar   5 + Durability ÷ 10 (seconds) — usually ≈ 5.7 seconds Package bar / placing a packaged structure   0.5 seconds Energy to demolish   10 + Durability ÷ 2 — usually ≈ 13.5 Max Durability   7 (original-game scale) · materials with a «building durability» attribute add/subtract more (2 per level) · minimum 2 Hammer wear per build/modification   4 Structures built before the scale change were converted automatically — their Durability ratio and the time left before they decay away are unchanged. Example finishing times (after the build bar ends) — these are the original game's values, unchanged; each blueprint's time is shown on the build screen: Structure   Finishing time   Max helpers House   3 hours   6 Brick House   2 hours   8 Barracks   1 hour 30 minutes   6 Small Box   30 minutes   2 Tent   15 minutes   2 Wide Box   16 hours   3 Expert Workbench · Kitchen   16 hours   4 Bonfire · Personal Storage   instant   —

Help with Finalization (anyone but the owner): cuts the remaining time by total finishing time ÷ (max helpers + 1) · once per person per site · 3 helps per day Instant Construction (owner): pay Warp Gems based on the time left — the number on the button is what is actually charged · not enough Gems = you can't skip · if skipping fails after the Gems are taken, they are refunded (Warp Gems can be exchanged from Durango Coins in the shop — see Warp Gems) Time left   Warp Gems up to 1 minute   1 15 minutes   15 30 minutes   30 1 hour   60 3 hours   122 1 day   780 7 days   3,000 Prices between these points scale linearly.

You can always put materials into someone else's site, and press Help with Finalization You can press Build on someone else's site only if you have learned that blueprint — if not, the game says you can't build in the owner's place (you may still add materials), and the site owner has to press Build

A furnished house interior Houses (and Barracks) can be dragged to size; materials scale with size · the maximum size follows your house-size skill (2 × 2 tiles to start) · houses can be rotated A finished house comes with one Basic Wooden Door Frame at the first wall slot (the corner of the front wall) — you can walk in and out right away (older houses without a door got one automatically) · move or remove it on the Wall Decoration screen Modification: swap the materials of a part (walls, floor, roof, pillars) — old materials return to your bag, then you must wait out the modification time (table below) · parts can also get a new texture, which is instant Wall Decoration: touch a finished house → Manage Wall Items button; place doors, windows and wall decorations from your bag — one item fits in one place only · take them back any time (owner only) · a house whose top floor has no roof has no wall to decorate on that floor Extend: House and Brick House can go up to 3 floors Extension   T-Stones 1 → 2 floors   10,000 2 → 3 floors   20,000 If an extension fails (for example two extensions at the same time), the T-Stones are refunded. A house modification has to run its full time — meanwhile the structure is translucent and you can't use it (there is no skip button or friend help for modifications): Part modified   House   Barracks Walls · floor   1 hour   — Roof   1 hour   30 minutes Pillars   20 minutes   15 minutes

Furniture inside a house counts toward a Set Effect once all pieces of a set are present, and creates an Ambiance based on its style — use Look Around inside the house to receive the ambiance effect. Set   Pieces needed   Effect Kitchen   Cooking Storage · Cooking Countertop · Table   Unattended crafting (cooking) on the countertop in the house takes 35% less time Living Room   Sofa · Interior Brazier · 2 decorations   Faster energy recovery while resting in the house Bedroom   Table · Bed · Lighting   Faster fatigue recovery, health/life regen while resting in the house There are 6 ambiances: Cute Ambiance (higher max energy) · Fragrant Spring Ambiance (higher great-success chance when crafting) · Luxurious Ambiance · Fiery Ambiance (higher attack) · Gloomy Ambiance (animals' pre-emptive attack range shrinks) · Academic Ambiance (shorter skill research) The set menu opens when the house's Antibiotic is ≥ 20 · the ambiance menu opens when Comfort is ≥ 30

Workbenches Workbenches (kitchens, kilns, drying racks, …) are needed for workbench recipes; stand within 4 tiles. Some recipes (food, firing, drying, fertilizer) are unattended crafting — leave the job on the bench, go do something else, and collect the result when the time is up · cancelling returns the materials. See recipes in Crafting and Cooking. Workbenches, stoves, kilns and drying racks at level 60 get one extra job slot (compared with level 59).

House doors are wall decorations (the Basic Wooden Door Frame comes with the house · swap it for a wooden door etc. on the Wall Decoration screen). Gate-type structures can be opened/closed by touching them · on someone else's Domain you need the «Enter» permission to use the gate (this permission does not stop anyone walking into the Domain)

Touch your own structure → Demolish · wait for the bar (length depends on Durability, usually ≈ 6 seconds) · the animation follows the hammer in your hands (two-handed / one-handed / bare hands) — time and energy are the same Materials come back in proportion to Durability at the moment you demolish (badly decayed = fewer) · a site that was never built returns 100% Items in boxes/storage, reins in pens, wall decorations (doors, windows), workbench jobs (finished = the product · unfinished = materials back) and incoming cargo all go to the demolisher's bag · pets in pens go back to their owner Demolishing a house also demolishes every piece of furniture inside it (all floors) — materials and contents go to your bag, nothing is left floating Returned items enter your bag even if it is full (nothing is lost) Domain owners who touch someone else's structure on their own Domain get Demolish and Package options · demolish = materials go to the demolisher's bag · the contents are mailed back to the original builder · package = see Domain

Packageable structures: touch → Package (the owner · or the owner of the Domain it stands on — see Domain). It becomes a «Packaged Construction» item or a Moving Box in your bag. Packaging your own structure keeps everything — level, Durability, name, box contents · Durability does not drop while you carry it · place it somewhere new without rebuilding. Item   Value Packaging fee inside your own Domain / your clan's Domain   free Packaging fee outside a Domain   100 × structure level T-Stones (e.g. level 50 = 5,000) Packaging bar   0.5 seconds The package's name, description and icon are those of the structure inside (not an empty box) — in your bag, boxes, mail and the market You pay before packaging · if packaging fails you get the fee back · not enough T-Stones = you can't package, nothing is lost Structures at zero Durability can't be packaged — repair or demolish only Packaging a house demolishes the furniture you built inside it back into your bag, like demolishing the house · furniture other players built in the house is mailed back whole to its builder (as a package if it can be packaged, otherwise as materials by Durability + its contents) with a notice

Placing follows the same rules as building (Where you can build) · a structure packaged while rotated places with the same direction and grid you saw · on a Tamed Island it can only be placed inside your own Domain It keeps the Durability it had when packaged (it is not refilled) · shop items are always full Decay follows where you place it — on a Domain = the in-Domain rule (7 days, never vanishes) · outside a Domain = the outside rule, and the 10-minute "nobody uses it" clock starts when you place it (Decay) The Personal Stage (sold in the shop) can be placed anywhere, not only on a personal island · touching it opens the dance minigame; there is no crafting buff, whatever the in-game item description says

sec.h: Unfinished sites outside your land are cleaned up
sec.x: A construction site that is not finished yet (the site is placed but the materials aren't all in, or Build hasn't been pressed) and stands outside your own and your clan's Domain (including the Domain of a system character) is removed automatically if nobody touches it for 24 hours. «Touching» = placing the site · opening the site window · putting in materials · pressing Build — each one restarts the 24 hours Every material you put in is returned by mail (the same items) with the title «Construction site outside your land was cleaned up — materials returned» (Thai in game); open your mailbox and claim it Not affected: finished structures (normal decay rules apply — Decay) · sites whose finishing timer is running · sites on your own or your clan's Domain · sites on another player's Domain (for example a friend who gave you the «Build» permission) · sites on the tutorial island The server checks while players are nearby, so a site nobody walks past is removed when someone gets close (the time keeps counting meanwhile)

Two standing flags are buildable by everyone from the build menu, with no skill to learn first: the Thai Flag and the Durango:Reborn Flag (a white flag with the server icon). 1×1, can stand indoors or outdoors, rotates in 4 directions · no materials are specified and there is no finishing time · can be packaged and moved You need the PC game version 3.1.5 or later to see the flag cloth · on mobile the flag itself is not visible yet

sec.h: Houses reappear when you come back
sec.x: Walk far away and run back — your house and nearby structures load again as you approach, no relog needed. Still can't see a structure or animal that should be there → type /reload (or /รีโหลด) in chat and the server re-sends the structures and animals around you · once per 30 seconds · the reply is Thai-only · if it is still invisible after that, the model file for it is missing on the server (not a connection problem) — tell the staff

sec.h: No lag in areas packed with buildings
sec.x: Walking around islands packed with houses and structures (e.g. Tamed Islands, Safe Houses) no longer makes the server lag — other players and animals move smoothly and your actions respond right away. Houses and structures still load completely and look the same Box contents load when you touch/open a box, not in advance Nothing for players to do

Structures taking damage from animal or player attacks A time limit to finish a construction site — unfinished sites on your own or your clan's Domain stay indefinitely (outside a Domain, untouched sites are cleaned up — see Unfinished sites outside your land are cleaned up)

d: Declare a Domain as your own land and expand it up to 6 plots (8 on a Tamed Island) — structures there decay slowly and others can do nothing without permission

sec.x: Private Domain flag A Domain is land a player declares as their own, made of plots of 4 × 4 tiles. Structures on your own Domain decay far more slowly (7 days and they never vanish — see Decay), and nobody else can build, demolish or open boxes there without permission.

Declare a Domain on an allowed island — free Expand Domain one plot at a time (costs T-Stones) · reduce unused plots · cancel the whole Domain Manage Permissions — choose what other players may do on your Domain Declare a Tamed Island Domain on your own personal island Clans can declare a clan Enclave (Clan) Visit another player's Domain with the Domain button in their player-info popup (below)

Go to the spot on the island, open the Domain page and press Declare on that plot Expand: pick a plot adjacent to your Domain (up/down/left/right); you must be on the same island as the Domain Reduce: pick the plot to give up — you cannot remove the last plot (cancel instead), and the Domain must not split in two Permissions: Domain Permissions page → tick what others may do You cannot declare or expand over another player's structure — a plot with someone else's structure on it (including an unfinished site) is refused · discarded item bundles do not block [!warn] Reducing plots or cancelling a Domain = the structures on those plots (yours and your friends') become outside-Domain structures at once — any that nobody has used for over 10 minutes vanish almost immediately · always package them first (Decay)

Island   Can declare? Village islands · Civilized Island   yes (normal Domain) Your own Tamed Island   yes (Tamed Island Domain) Safe House Island · Unstable Island · training islands   no Lawless Island   no (you can still place bonfires/temporary things under the outside-Domain rules) Another player's Tamed Island that you are visiting   no

sec.h: You must stand at the plot when declaring
sec.x: When you declare, you must stand close to the plot — within 4 tiles of its edge — and the plot must be on the island, otherwise the game refuses («You must stand at the plot you want to declare» / «This plot is outside the island», Thai in game) · Expanding has no distance check, you only need to be on the same island as the Domain

Item   Value Plot size   4 × 4 tiles Domains per player   1 per island Max plots (normal Domain)   6 Max plots (Tamed Island Domain)   8 Max plots (clan Enclave)   8 per Enclave Declaring (player)   free Declaring (clan Enclave)   10,000 × number of Enclaves after declaring — paid from the clan fund Expanding on a Tamed Island   free Expansion cost for a player's normal Domain: From → to   T-Stones 1 → 2 plots   2,500 2 → 3 plots   2,500 3 → 4 plots   5,000 4 → 5 plots   7,500 5 → 6 plots   12,500 Total 1 → 6   30,000 After reducing, expanding back is free up to the largest size you ever reached. Clan Enclave: declaring and expanding are paid from the clan fund (not the T-Stones of whoever presses the button) — expansion per plot 10,000 · 11,000 · 12,000 · 13,000 · 14,000 · 15,000 · 17,000 (size 1→2 … 7→8) · the clan must be level 5+, and the total number of Enclaves is capped by clan level — see Clan [!tip] Expanding on a Tamed Island is completely free — if you want lots of room without spending T-Stones, build on your own Tamed Island (Islands) · structures and furniture on a Tamed Island never decay (Decay)

Manage Domain The owner can always do everything · others can only do what the owner allows: Permission   Effect Enter   use gates on the Domain (does not stop anyone walking in) Use   use structures — open storage/pens, craft, mannequins Give   put items into storage · put reins/animals into pens · add incense Take   take items/animals out · collect from wells/fish traps Build   build structures on the Domain Demolish   demolish structures Boxes and workbenches need several permissions at once — see Boxes, workbenches and pens A newly declared Domain has every permission off — the owner turns them on in the permissions page · older Domains keep what they had You can also set permissions per item (Furniture Rights) — this opens that one item even when the Domain permissions are off · you can set a daily limit on how many items others may take (a Friend slot left without a number = friends can't take anything) Structures others build on your Domain (friends, or anyone you gave «Build») follow the in-Domain decay rule — 7 days and they never vanish, even if you remove the permission later · if you don't want them, demolish or package them yourself (below) [!warn] A normal box placed outside any Domain can be opened and emptied by anyone — keep valuables on your own Domain, or use a Personal Box, which only its owner can open (Storage)

The Domain Permissions page has Friend and Close Friend tabs, separate from «others» — tick the same 6 permissions from the table above for each group. Applies to player Domains and Tamed Island Domains · Clan Enclaves still use rank permissions as before Which group a friend belongs to comes from what the Domain owner set in their friend list (Friend / Close Friend) Friends always use the Friends tab instead of the «others» permissions — if you opened permissions for others but ticked nothing on the Friends tab, your friends can do nothing The Friends tabs start with every permission off, for new and existing Domains alike — tick them yourself if you want friends to have access Per-item permissions (Furniture Rights) also have Friend / Close Friend slots

sec.h: Farm plots and gates on a Domain
sec.x: On your Domain, others can sow, water, fertilize or uproot/harvest a farm plot only if they have all 3 permissions Use + Give + Take (or you opened that plot's own per-item permission) — without them the plot's buttons can't be pressed · whoever built the plot can always use it (Farming) Others can open/close gates on your Domain only with the «Enter» permission · walking onto the Domain is never blocked A sprinkler on someone else's Domain needs the «Use» permission

sec.h: Boxes, workbenches and pens on someone else's Domain
sec.x: Structures that hold items or animals (boxes, cabinets, baskets, Personal Storage, workbenches, kilns, bonfires, drying racks, pens, mannequins, wells, fish traps, censers) standing on someone else's Domain can only be used by the Domain owner, the player who built that item, and players who have the permission matching what they want to do — without it the button can't be pressed Structure   Permission needed Boxes, cabinets, baskets — open, store, take, sort, discard from the box   Use + Take, both, for everything Workbenches, kilns, bonfires, drying racks — craft, start/collect/cancel jobs   Use + Give + Take, all three Personal Storage · pens · censers   per button: open/view = Use · put in = Give · take out = Take Wells · fish traps (collecting)   Take Farm plots · gates   see above Outside any Domain nothing changed: normal boxes, pens, wells and crafting at workbenches are open to anyone · Personal Boxes, Personal Storage and unattended crafting on a workbench are owner-only The player who built the item can always use it, even on someone else's Domain Your animals kept in someone else's pen — you can always take them back, feed them and give them tasks Reins left in someone else's taming pen on someone else's Domain: if the Domain owner removes your «Take» permission you can't get them back yourself — ask the Domain owner to take them out for you

The clan leader (or a rank with the right) can declare the clan's Enclave on village/Civilized islands once the clan is level 5 or higher · declaring and expanding are paid from the clan fund (numbers above) · members get permissions by rank · non-members use the «others» permissions like a player Domain · members' structures on the Enclave follow the in-Domain decay rule. See Clan for details.

sec.h: No wild animals spawn on your Domain
sec.x: Wild animals do not spawn or settle on player Domains, clan Enclaves and Domains on a Tamed Island, nor within 12 tiles around their border. Animals whose home was already inside the zone move out on their own · animals chasing you can still follow you in, so stay alert Fixed-spot animals, rift guards and quest animals still appear where they did before Newly declared or expanded Domains take effect within a few seconds See Animals for details.

Tap another player → open the player-info popup → press the Domain button to warp into the middle of their Domain on a stable (Civilized) island — no sailing needed (Warp holes and rifts). Anyone can use it, it is free, and the owner does not need to be online · if they have no land on a stable island the game tells you so Works once you have left the Safe House (it can't be used from the tutorial island or the Safe House) The destination island's normal travel rules apply What you can open, use or build there depends on the permissions the owner set Clan Enclaves and clan warpoints can't be visited yet · another player's Tamed Island can only be visited through the Tamed Island visit button (a Supporter's private Tamed Island that the owner has opened)

You cannot declare a Domain here Player structures on this island follow the outside-Domain rule: they break within 1 day and vanish if nobody uses them for 10 minutes (Decay) Objects placed by the game itself (the village, camp workbenches) are not affected K's Domain (near the balloon above the camp): walking in shows the sign «K's Domain» · you can't declare over it, build, place or demolish there · K's balloon and motorbike work normally inside

sec.h: Domain owners and other players' structures
sec.x: A Domain owner (on a clan Enclave: a rank that can manage the Enclave) who touches a structure someone else built on their Domain gets: Demolish — materials go to the demolisher's bag · the contents are mailed back to the builder Package (packageable items · free) — the package goes into the Domain owner's bag and becomes the Domain owner's (wherever you place it, it is yours) · the builder loses that structure Contents (box/storage items, wall decorations, workbench jobs, incoming cargo, reins in taming pens) do not go into the package — they are mailed back to the builder · animals in pens go back to their owners · crops in farm plots are lost (as with demolishing) A custom name and the text/drawing on a sign are cleared · incense in a censer stays · a house keeps its Basic Wooden Door Frame Packaging a house: furniture you built yourself goes back to your bag · other players' furniture is mailed back whole to whoever built it (as a package if it can be packaged, otherwise as materials by Durability + its contents) The builder always gets a notice by mail, even with nothing inside (the mail is in Thai · structure names in it are the Korean in-game names) Structures with zero Durability (repair first) or not yet finished can't be packaged — they can be demolished Packaging (moving) a structure is free on your own Domain/your clan's Enclave · elsewhere 100 × level T-Stones (Building) [!warn] Building on someone else's Domain = its owner can demolish or package your structure
In the original game a Domain expired and had to be extended — this server does not have that yet: Domains never expire and have no daily maintenance fee; they last until the owner cancels them.

d: Structures lose Durability over time — on a Domain they break after 7 days (repairable) · outside a Domain they vanish after 1 day · on a Tamed Island they never decay · an unused bonfire dies out in 3 minutes and vanishes 1 minute later · repair with Building Repair Kits or instantly with Warp Gems

sec.x: Repair Every finished structure has Durability, which keeps dropping over time (even when nobody is around). How fast it drops and what happens at zero depends on where it stands — your own Domain is far safer (Domain).

Check a structure's condition on its info page (Durability / condition) Repair it with Building Repair Kits or Repair Now with Warp Gems → Durability is full again and the countdown restarts Package it (Building) — Durability does not drop while it sits in your bag · when placed again it keeps the Durability it had when packaged Pick up the item bundles left behind by structures that fell apart

Where it stands   Durability runs out in   At zero   Nobody uses it Any player's Domain (yours, a friend's, anyone's) · clan Enclave — no matter who built it   7 days   breaks and cannot be used until repaired — it does not vanish, contents stay   no effect Outside any Domain (every island) · Safe House Island   1 day   vanishes, contents drop as bundles on the ground   unused for 10 minutes → vanishes at once Everything on a Tamed Island (the shared Tamed Islands and Supporters' private Tamed Islands)   does not decay — Durability stays fixed   —   no effect Player-placed Bonfire · Large Bonfire · Cooking Bonfire (anywhere)   1 day   vanishes   the fire dies out in 3 minutes · out for 1 minute → vanishes (below) Interior Brazier (anywhere)   1 day   vanishes   no effect Bonfires and Interior Braziers always decay as in the last two rows, even on a Tamed Island.
