Durability drops in a straight line over that period regardless of its maximum (every structure takes the time in the table) The "nobody uses it" clock starts when construction finishes or when you place a packaged structure (shop items included) · it counts as used when someone actually does something with it, e.g. opens a box, puts in/takes out items, crafts at a workbench, lights a fire, opens a gate, repairs it Unfinished construction sites do not decay or vanish If nobody is nearby, the removal happens when someone next comes close to that area, but the time keeps running the whole while When the owner reduces or

A construction site that is not finished yet, stands outside your own and your clan's Domain, and has not been touched by anyone for 24 hours is removed automatically — the materials you put in are mailed back · finished structures are not affected (the decay rules above apply to them) · details in Building

Player-placed bonfires (Bonfire · Large Bonfire · Cooking Bonfire) are short-lived — on every island, your own Domain included State   What happens Lit, but nobody uses it for 3 minutes   the fire dies out and it becomes an unlit bonfire Out (died out · Extinguish Fire pressed · put out by heavy rain/heavy snow) for 1 minute   the bonfire vanishes · anything left on it drops as a bundle on the ground Using it = opening its menu · roasting/crafting · starting unattended crafting · resting next to it while it is lit · lighting it → the 3 minutes start over · anyone's use counts, not just the owner's While it is out, only lighting it before the minute is up saves it (just opening the menu doesn't extend the time) · light it too late and you get a Thai-only message saying it has been out too long and can't be relit An unattended crafting job on it → it neither dies out nor vanishes until the job is done, then the timers continue from that moment — come back for your items An unlit bonfire: no roasting/crafting/starting jobs (Thai-only message «กองไฟดับอยู่ — จุดไฟก่อน», "the bonfire is out — light it first"), but finished jobs can still be collected · you can still sit there, but it is a plain rest: no warming up Resting at an island's own bonfire (e.g. in a camp) with a lit player bonfire within resting range also counts as using that bonfire Not covered by this rule: Interior Brazier (decays in 1 day as in the table) · bonfires placed by the game itself (never die out or vanish
Durability left   Condition more than 40%   normal more than 10%   old more than 0   worn 0   broken

sec.h: When it breaks on your own Domain
sec.x: Only Repair and Demolish remain in its menu (it can't be packaged) Your own box: its owner can still open it and take items out, but can't store anything until it is repaired Personal Storage, workbenches, pens and everything else can't be used until repaired — contents are safe · nobody else can use it at all It never vanishes by itself; you can repair it any time

sec.h: When it vanishes outside a Domain
sec.x: Everything inside — box contents, every storage tab, reins in pens, wall decorations — drops as Abandoned Objects (bundles on the ground) where the structure stood. Item   Value Items per bundle   up to 80 (more items = several bundles) Bundle lifetime   24 hours Who can pick it up   anyone (touch the bundle → Pick Up) The bundles hold everything: box contents · wall decorations · workbench jobs (finished = the product · unfinished = the materials) · incoming cargo

Building Repair Kit Touch a structure whose Durability is not full → Repair (stand within 4 tiles) Choose Building Repair Kits from your bag whose total repair power ≥ the required repair power Wait for the 5-second bar → Durability is always restored to full (no failure roll) and decay starts over · the kits are used up Anyone can repair a structure; you don't have to be the owner. Kit   Repair power Budget Building Repair Kit   30 Standard Building Repair Kit   90 Quality Building Repair Kit   150 Required repair power depends on the structure type and level (minimum 5) — examples: Structure   Level 1   Level 30   Level 50   Level 60 Small Box   5   10   30   40 House   5   20   40   60 Personal Box   5   30   60   80 Personal Storage   30   80   120   140 Energy used to repair = required repair power × 0.8 [!tip] Repair before Durability runs out — an outside structure repaired in time gets another full day · one on your Domain gets another 7 days The Repair option only appears on structures that can be repaired — tents, bonfires and house roofs can't be repaired (no option).

No repair kit? Press Repair Now in the repair window and pay Warp Gems instead. Cost = the required repair power, in Gems (the same number the confirm window shows) — e.g. a level 30 House (repair power 20) = 20 Gems · level 60 Personal Storage (140) = 140 Gems 5-second bar → full Durability · energy/fatigue are the same as repairing with kits Not enough Gems = no repair (the game says Gems are short and how many you need) · if the repair fails after the Gems are taken, they are refunded (with a message) Warp Gems can be exchanged from Durango Coins in the shop — see Warp Gems [!note] Max Durability uses the original-game scale (see Building) — decay times, conditions and the share of materials returned on demolish are unchanged · demolishing a badly decayed structure returns materials based on its real remaining Durability

d: Your bag holds 200 items (+ slots from worn bags) · Storage Boxes hold 80–300 depending on type and level · Personal Storage has tabs of 200, up to 10 tabs · items discarded on the ground last 30 minutes

sec.x: Personal Storage Items live in 4 places: your bag · Storage Boxes you built · Personal Storage (a tabbed warehouse) · and bundles on the ground when you discard things. How safe boxes and storage are depends on where they stand — see Domain and Decay.

Carry up to 200 items in your bag + extra slots from the bags/clothes you wear Build Storage Boxes or Personal Storage, then Store / Take Out / sort items Name and organize tabs in Personal Storage Discard items onto the ground as a bundle for yourself or others to pick up Package a box and move it — the contents go with it · free on your own Domain/clan Enclave · 100 × level T-Stones outside a Domain (Building)

Item   Value Maximum   200 items (every item counts; a stack of 10 = 10) When full you cannot receive new items (gathering, harvesting, drawing water, …) — the game says the bag is full and the extra is not received; it does not drop on the ground Items you get back (demolishing a structure, cancelling a job) still enter your bag when full, so nothing is lost If you already hold more than 200, nothing is taken away, but you cannot receive new items until you are below 200 [!tip] Before a long gathering trip, store what you don't need in a box — if your bag fills up on the way, whatever you gather won't go in

sec.h: Extra bag slots from worn items
sec.x: Bags and some clothes you are wearing add bag capacity — several pieces add up · some items and statuses add more too, e.g. [Event] Travel Luggage +20 · the bag window shows «count / maximum» with the new value and the server uses the same limit Worn item   Extra slots Leaf Bag   +2 Fabric Bag   +4 Small Bag · Cherry Blossom Bag · Bamboo Bag   +6 (Bamboo Bag at level 60 = +7) Secondary Bag   +9 Backpack   +13 (level 60 = +15) Recycled Bag   +15 Some clothes (e.g. Lightweight Collection Outfit · Heavy Construction Suit)   +1 to +4 by outfit and level If you take off the item while carrying more than the normal limit, your items don't disappear — the number turns red and you can't pick up anything new until you are back under the limit The Attach Pocket reform / «수납력» property on worn clothes or bags: level = extra slots (level 3 = +3 slots) · several pieces add up A piece at 0 durability gives no slots at all (including the bag's own slots) until repaired — the lost slots work like taking the item off (nothing is lost) · the number updates as soon as it breaks or the repair finishes

Small Box Personal Box Touch a box → Open Storage → drag items in (Store) / out (Take Out) · stand within 4 tiles Capacity depends on the box type and the box's level — at least 80 items, at most 300: Box   Capacity Basket · Small Box · Small Personal Box   80 Personal Box   80–110 (level 60 = 110) Large Box   90–130 (level 60 = 130) Wide Box   140–161 Some boxes only take certain kinds of items — e.g. Closet = clothing · Armory = weapons · Icebox = food/drinks · ordinary boxes can't hold reins · putting in the wrong kind is refused (Thai-only message) and the item stays in your bag Items that were already inside a box before this rule are not taken away Who can open it: Box stands on   Normal box   Personal Box (locked) Your Domain   you + people you gave permission   you + people you gave permission Someone else's Domain   the Domain owner · the box's builder · people with permission   the Domain owner · the box's builder · people with permission Outside any Domain   everyone   the box owner only A box on someone else's Domain needs both «Use» and «Take» to open it, store, take or discard from it — «Use» or «Give» alone is not enough · the box owner can also set per-item permissions and a daily limit on how many items others may take (Domain) [!tip] Want friends to drop items off without taking any out? Give them «Use» + «Take», then set the friends' daily take limit to 0 in that box's per-item permissions [!warn] A broken box (Durability at zero): its owner can still open

A large warehouse split into tabs you can name. Item   Value Capacity per tab   200 items Max tabs   10 (2,000 items total) Tab name   1–24 characters, no duplicates A new one comes with one tab · you can create/rename/reorder tabs · only empty tabs can be removed Only the owner can manage tabs Outside a Domain only the owner can use it · on a Domain it follows the «Use/Give/Take» permissions

Moving Box Select items in your bag → Discard → they become an Abandoned Object (a bundle on the ground) at the chosen spot. Item   Value Fee (from your bag)   10 T-Stones per discard Where the bundle goes   within 4 tiles (none chosen = under your feet) One bundle holds   80 items (extra returns to your bag) Bundle lifetime   30 minutes from the last time items were added Bundles from structures that fell apart   24 hours Discarding again on the same tile adds to the existing bundle and renews its time Anyone can pick it up — touch the bundle → Pick Up · an empty bundle disappears Equipped or locked items cannot be discarded Discarding from a box/Personal Storage/pet bag drops a bundle under your feet (box/storage: you must stand within 4 tiles and have permission to take from it · counts toward the daily take limit) · discarding from a ground bundle itself destroys the item Ground bundles block building just like structures (pick the bundle up first, then build over it — Building), but they do not block Domain declarations [!tip] To hand something to a friend standing next to you, discard it and let them pick it up — but anyone else can grab it too. If it isn't urgent, Mail is safer

sec.h: Nothing is lost when structures are demolished or collapse
sec.x: Demolishing a box/storage/workbench/house: contents · wall decorations · workbench jobs · incoming cargo all go to the demolisher's bag (when a Domain owner demolishes someone else's structure, the contents are mailed back to the builder) A Domain owner packages a box/storage you built on their Domain → all its contents are mailed back to you (Domain) A structure outside a Domain that collapses: all of the above drops as bundles on the ground (Decay)

sec.h: A failed take puts the items back
sec.x: If you take items out of a box, Personal Storage, finished work on a workbench or a pet bag and they can't go into your bag (for example when the server is busy), the items go back where they were, with the message «take failed, the item is still in the …» (Thai in game) — just try again. Item bundles on the ground: if taking from the bundle fails, the items are dropped back as a bundle on the same spot Items dropped on death: if they can't go into your bag, they return to the spot where you died, with the message «could not collect the items dropped on death — they are still at your death spot, try again» If they truly can't be put back, they are held for the staff to check instead of vanishing silently

d: Fight animals bare handed, with melee weapons, bows or crossbows — damage depends on attack, the move you use, and armor penetration against the animal's defense · skill moves spend Stamina · bows shoot 6 tiles · training dummies · the catapult · character combat stats, auto-dodge and auto-block · fighting players on the Lawless Islands

sec.x: Dinosaurs and wild animals are your food, your materials and your biggest danger. Combat on this server follows the original game's rules: every hit starts from weapon attack × the move's multiplier, then compares your armor penetration with the animal's defense. The colored area an animal draws on the ground while winding up is exactly where it will hit — step out in time and it misses. A hunter slashing a raptor

Fight bare handed, with one-handed weapons (axe · knife/sword · blunt weapon), two-handed weapons, spears, bows and crossbows Use heavy hits, flurries and sweeping moves that hit several animals at once (these must be learned from the combat skill tree — see Skills) Stagger an animal so the attack it is winding up is cancelled; make it stunned / collapse to capture it (see Taming) Break body parts (head · body · legs · tail) to slow an animal down or weaken its attacks Use green weapon tags to make animals bleed (see Tags) Shoot bows and crossbows up to 6 tiles (the farther, the weaker) — see Bow and crossbow range Practice on the training dummies and the punch machine in the Safe House and see your real damage numbers at no cost Skill moves and the roll spend your Stamina bar — see Move stamina On the Lawless Islands (level 56+) you can fight other players — see Lawless Islands (PvP) · play last-one-standing matches on Brawl Island (level 50+) — see Brawl Island

Tap an animal to target it, then press Attack  — your character walks into range and swings A weapon's basic attack is always available · special moves (heavy hit, flurry, stab, sweep, strike, aimed shot, quick shot) must be learned first Watch the colored area under the animal while it winds up — run out of it before the attack lands to dodge Animals you hit will turn and fight; some herbivores run away instead (see Wild animals) · if it can reach you it always strikes back, even when you stand in the safe zone around a Harbor or have lured it far from home — see When an animal is hit Standing on a water tile (even ankle-deep) you cannot attack — bows, crossbows, combat skills, every target including players · your pets don't attack or use attack skills while you stand in water either (riding a pet into the water counts as being in the water) · the roll still works · get back on land to fight You can hit an animal from somewhere it can't walk to (a small island, a sandbar cut off by water, a cliff), but it will lose interest and walk home, its health recovering at the normal rate — see When an animal is hit

Numbers are the move's damage multiplier (1.0 = normal hit) · several numbers = several strikes Weapon   Normal hit   Special moves (multiplier) Bare Handed (attack 40)   1.0   Kick 0.8 · heavy hit 1.3 · punch combo 0.6 ×3 One-Handed (axe · knife/sword · hammer)   1.0   Heavy hit 2.2 · flurry 0.9 / 1.1 / 1.33 · stab 2.8 Two-Handed   1.0   Heavy hit 2.2 · sweep 1.1 / 1.6 · strike 2.5 Spear   1.0   Heavy thrust 2.2 · dash thrust 1.1 ×3 / 1.2 Bow / Crossbow   1.0   Quick shot 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.22 · aimed shot 2.1 [!note] Holding a weapon uses the weapon's attack (the bare-hand 40 is not added), then your character's attack bonus is added · axes, swords and hammers share the same move multipliers; they differ in their mastery skills

Damage = attack × move multiplier × penetration multiplier × direction multiplier × critical Attack = the attack of the weapon in your hand (bare hands 40) + your character's attack bonus (tags, built-in gear bonuses, food, titles, house ambiance and your stats — every 5 points of Strength above 10 = +1 attack) — the same number as on the character screen (Character stats) Penetration multiplier = 2.2 to the power of ((your armor penetration − animal defense) ÷ 100) · your armor penetration = the weapon's (bare hands 40) + your character's penetration bonus (every 5 points of Strength above 10 = +1) Difference 0 = ×1 · penetration ahead by 100 or more = ×2.2 (cap) · defense ahead by 100 or more = ×0.45 (floor) Animal defense grows with level (usually level × 5, e.g. Raptor Lv10 = 50) and is multiplied by the island's Unstable Index Hit chance = 50% + move accuracy × 45% (normal moves of bare hands, swords, axes, blunt weapons and spears = 95% · bow normal shot ≈ 84% · crossbow normal shot ≈ 86%) · heavy moves −4% · + 0.1% per point of your character's Accuracy above 100 · always between 35% and 99% Animal dodge — after your hit lands, the animal still has a chance to dodge = animal Evasion × 0.1% × 100 ÷ your Accuracy (max 40%) · most animals have Evasion = level × 5 · a dodge shows «Dodged», the animal loses no health, your weapon doesn't wear and you get no exp (same as a miss) · so Accuracy works two ways: your hit chance + cutting the target's dodge · animals with broken

Some skill lines give moves a chance for that hit to ignore the animal's defense completely (counted as if the animal had 0 defense — direction, critical and body parts still apply as normal) · skills covering the same move add up Skill   Moves affected   Per level (3 levels) Backstab (penetration line)   One-handed stab   +10% Sword specialization   One-/two-handed normal and special moves   +6% Spear specialization   All spear moves   +6% Bow specialization   All bow moves   +10%

Bows and crossbows shoot up to 6 tiles with every shooting move, but the farther the target, the weaker the hit Distance from you to the target's edge   Damage Up to 3.75 tiles   Full 100% 3.75 → 6 tiles   Falls in a straight line down to 60% Beyond 6 tiles   60% The aimed shot (bow and crossbow) does not fall off — full damage at any range · normal shots and quick shots follow the table Measured from you to the edge of the target's body at the moment the shot lands — big animals aren't penalized for being big Same for animals, players on the Lawless Islands (the ×0.35 for shooting players still multiplies on top) and training dummies · melee moves and accuracy are not affected If you tap a target farther than 6 tiles, your character walks up to the 6-tile edge and shoots there = 60% damage — walk closer yourself first if you want full damage

sec.h: Arrows and stones you can see
sec.x: With game version 3.1.5 or newer (PC and Android), shooting a bow, crossbow or sling shows the projectile flying from the shooter to the target — arrows that hit stay stuck in the target for about 5 seconds, then disappear · players around you see your arrows and you see theirs · damage, accuracy and range are unchanged, only the visuals are new

Combat moves spend Stamina (full bar 100 · refills by itself at about 5 per second — the Stamina-regeneration skills make it faster, see Character stats) · each move's cost is shown in its description · applies to every target: animals, players (PvP) and training dummies Basic attacks (a weapon's base move) always go out, even at zero Stamina — they take whatever is left Every skill move and the roll needs enough Stamina — if you don't have it the move doesn't fire, you see «Not enough Stamina», no cooldown is spent and nothing is deducted · wait for the bar to refill and press again Basic attacks in a row cost Stamina too: one-handed swings cost 5–6 in about 1 second, more than the refill, so the bar slowly drops · bows/crossbows drain faster (12 per 1.8 seconds) · two-handed basic attacks cost less than the refill (the bar doesn't drop) While you see «Exhausted — sit and rest» or «Too fatigued …», every move including basic attacks is unavailable until you rest The skills «Roll: Stamina I–III» and «Barrage: Stamina I–III» cut that move's cost by 6% per level Move   Stamina cost   Cooldown (seconds) Basic attack: one-handed · two-handed · spear   5–6 · 8–9 · 7   — Basic attack: bow · crossbow · bare hands   12 · 12 · 0   — Roll   35   7 One-handed: heavy hit · flurry · stab   25–27 · 31–33 · 30–32   8.4–9.2 · 23.5–25.7 · 11.8–12.9 Two-handed: heavy hit · sweep · strike   31–35 · 50–59 · 35–39   12.6–13.5 · 32.2–35.8 · 16.4–18.3 Spear: heavy thrust · dash thrust   37 · 50   1

Every hit adds "blow power" to the animal's gauge. When the gauge reaches the species' stagger resistance, the animal staggers and the attack it is winding up is cancelled, then the gauge starts over · if it isn't hit for 4 seconds, the gauge resets Blow power per hit   Value Bow · bare hand · one-handed · crossbow (normal hit)   60 · 80 · 90 · 100 Two-handed (normal hit) · heavy hit · stab   120 · 150 · 180 Two-handed strike / second sweep swing   240 Animal   Resistance   One-handed normal hits needed Compsognathus · Phenacodus   140   2 Raptor   420   5 Sabertooth · Direwolf   560   7 Mammoth   1,120   13 Tyrannosaurus   1,575   18

Every move has its own hit area (circle · cone · rectangle) and the server checks each hit against it Area moves (flurry · sweep · stab · strike · punch combo) can hit several animals at once, up to 6 per swing · only animals on the island you're standing on · on a Lawless Island they hit enemy players too (6 targets in total) Animal attacks are cones/rectangles taken from their real moves (e.g. a raptor's tail swipe hits behind it) · the yellow/red area on screen = where the hit really lands

Direction: most animals take ×0.8 from the front · ×1.0 from the sides · ×1.2 from behind (Tyrannosaurus is reversed: front ×1.2 · back ×0.8) · you also take ×1.2 when an animal hits you from behind Body parts: each hit lands on the head/body/legs/tail at random depending on the direction. Each part has its own health; when it breaks: Broken legs → the animal walks/runs at 60% speed and is easier to hit Broken head or tail → the animal hits weaker or misses more often Broken parts heal by themselves after 10 minutes · when butchering, items from broken parts come out halved (except meat) Axe mastery skills add +6% body-part damage per level

Some green tags on weapons/gear make animals bleed (health drains over time — if it dies you get a normal carcass) or make animals that hit you miss more often · bleeding does not stagger or stun · see Tags for the tag list

Animals use the same formula: animal attack × 2.2 to the power of ((animal penetration − your defense) ÷ 100) · your defense = the defense of every armor piece + defense bonuses from skills/tags/gear/food/titles (the same value as on the character screen) · armor reduces damage but never blocks it completely; high-level animals hit very hard Animal   Your defense   Damage taken Raptor Lv10   0   35 Raptor Lv10   50   24 Sabertooth Lv40   100   176 Mammoth Lv50   150   466 Tyrannosaurus Lv60   300   952 After the damage is worked out there is still a chance to auto-dodge (no damage at all) and to auto-block (less damage) — dodge is rolled first, block only if you didn't dodge A hit that really lands (no dodge, no block) also has a 5% chance to knock your character down for a moment (about 2 seconds) — gear with the «Knockdown Resistance Buff» property lowers this by 1% per tag level (down to 0%), while properties that lower knockdown resistance raise it by 1% per level (Item properties) · animals only — players hitting each other don't knock down

sec.h: How much defense and blocking help
sec.x: A Lv30 character wearing armor with 122.5 total defense, holding a Lv30 two-handed stone axe (attack 154) · damage per hit (from the side, no critical) Animal   Armor only   + all Defense skills (+100 → 222.5)   Armor + block   All skills + block Raptor Lv30   54   25   8   1 Sabertooth Lv40   176   92   130   46 Mammoth Lv50   466   391   420   345 A block removes weapon attack × 0.3 = 154 × 0.3 ≈ 46 per blocked hit · at least 1 damage remains All Defense skills + all max-Health skills (Health 472 → 722): a Lv30 Raptor needs 9 → 29 hits to kill you · a Lv40 Sabertooth 3 → 8 · a Lv50 Mammoth still 2 [!warn] Animals Lv40 and above can kill a lightly armored player in 1–3 hits — go as a team, use heavy moves to stagger, and dodge the colored areas in time

An animal that has picked you shows its mood: an icon over its head (about to chase / fighting / running away), it turns to look at its target, and its body color shifts towards red with each level Level   When   Message on screen Calm   No target   — Excited   Has spotted you and is about to chase   «… is excited» Attacking   Chasing you (you haven't hit it)   «… is attacking» Angry   You hit it within the last 20 seconds   «… is angry» Furious   Angry and health at 50% or less   «… is furious» Final stand   Has a target and health at 20% or less   «… is making a final stand» The message appears only for the player the animal has picked, when the level goes up or it switches to a new target (not repeated within 15 seconds) · the color change is seen by everyone looking at that animal It is only a warning signal — the animal's strength and behavior are unchanged

Every time an animal lands a hit, you have an auto-dodge chance = Evasion × 0.1% × 100 ÷ the attacker's Accuracy (max 40%) — on a dodge you see «Dodged», lose no health, your character staggers aside briefly in the hit direction (animal hits and PvP), and the Defense category gets the same exp as dodging with a roll Evasion   Dodge chance (attacker Accuracy 100 · animal up to Lv20) 0 (default)   0% 30   3% 150   15% 400 or more   40% (cap) Animal Accuracy is mostly level × 5 (multiplied by the island Index) but never counts below 100 — animals up to Lv20 never make you dodge more than the table · a Lv40 animal (Accuracy 200) halves your dodge · Lv60 leaves a third — e.g. Evasion 115: Lv20 = 11.5% · Lv40 = 5.8% · Lv60 = 3.8% PvP uses the attacker's Accuracy (no minimum) — an attacker with Accuracy 150 against Evasion 115 = 7.7% · an attacker below 100 Accuracy lets the target dodge more Evasion comes from some gear (e.g. the improved melee combat outfit), tags, titles, food or your Agility stat (every 5 points above 10 = +1) — no skill level gives Evasion yet Works with every weapon, bare hands included

Hold a melee weapon (sword/knife · axe · blunt weapon · spear) that still has Durability, and when an animal hits you (and you didn't auto-dodge) you have a chance to block and take less damage — no button, nothing to press Block chance = 5% + 0.25% × Defense category level (max 20% — exactly at category Lv60) Damage removed = the attack of the weapon you hold × 0.3 (your character's attack bonus is not included) · at least 1 damage remains On screen it shows as the reduced damage number like a normal hit (no «blocked» text) The blocked part wears your weapon by half of the amount blocked (like when you hit) · armor only wears from the remaining damage A blocked hit gives Defense exp equal to a roll dodge, instead of the exp for taking a hit Bare hands, bows, crossbows = can't block · blocking doesn't stagger the animal or counter-attack Defense category level   Block chance 1   5.25% 30   12.5% 60   20%
Hitting an animal repeatedly drains its stun gauge until it freezes (stunned) or collapses with stars over its head. It can't attack during that time and can be captured — see Taming

sec.h: Training dummies and the punch machine
sec.x: The Safe House has 4 kinds of training dummy — Target · Scarecrow · Training Set · Punching Bag — and a Punch Machine, so you can try weapons and moves before heading out to hunt Tap a dummy and choose Attack! to enter combat mode and target it, then hit it with your normal moves — the damage number pops up on the dummy (people watching see the same number) Damage = your raw damage with the same formula as hitting animals (weapon, stats, skills, move, tags), but a dummy has no armor, never dodges and never makes you miss · critical hits and heavy moves work as usual Hitting a dummy gives no exp · your weapon doesn't wear · the dummy never breaks, dies or drops anything · it doesn't put you in the combat state Area moves aimed at an animal don't sweep dummies, and hits on a dummy don't sweep animals The Punch Machine costs 100 T Stone per try — the number it shows and ranks is the real damage with the same formula as above (the old ranking, which used the previous formula, has been cleared)

The catapult you can climb onto now really fires at enemies: Load it — tap the catapult, choose «Load Projectile» and pick big items tagged «big chunk» (for example Stone Chunk, Marble, Obsidian, Granite, Basalt, Large Skull) — 1 item = 1 shot, up to 400 shots (shown as «Projectile n/400») · you need the right to deposit items at that catapult Fire — sit in it and aim at a spot 3–7.5 tiles away · a warning circle appears on the ground about 2 seconds before the shot lands · at most one shot every 5 seconds, and it can't fire when it is empty Impact — hits every target within about 2.25 tiles of the impact point (up to 20 targets, nearest first) Hits   Result Wild animals   130 + 0.8 × the catapult's level damage (penetration 200 + level) · no critical · your own weapon and skills are not used Players on the Lawless Islands   Normal PvP rules (party, clan, allied clans and players still under their arrival shield aren't hit) · damage uses the PvP penetration table × 0.15, then halved = ×0.075 Whoever sits in the catapult inside the circle   Takes 60% Structures   Not damaged yet

You can hit players only on the Lawless Islands (open from level 56) and in Brawl Island matches (level 50+ — Brawl Island) — on every other island your only enemies are animals Same moves as against animals, but the damage formula against players is a PvP set of its own: gradual defense curve · 4% base critical chance · skill-category bonuses don't apply · kind-of-move multiplier ×0.8 (melee, area moves included) / ×0.35 (bow, crossbow — long shots also fall off with range), then halved again ×0.5 — all numbers at Damage in PvP · the target can still roll, auto-dodge and auto-block as usual Party members, clanmates and allied clans can't hit each other · players are never stunned by players · no exp for hitting players Everything else (arrival shield · what drops when you die) is on Lawless Islands (PvP)

The accuracy value on weapons themselves is not used for hit chance yet (hit chance comes from the move + your character's Accuracy · animal evasion is now used — see Animal dodge) · knockback moves have no push effect · there is no manual guard move (only auto-block)

d: Five level 60 islands where players can fight each other — open from Lv56 · who can hit whom · damage · the arrival shield · what you drop when you die · plus Brawl Island, last-one-standing matches for up to 16 players (Lv50+)

sec.x: On normal islands players can't hurt each other — your only enemies are animals. The exception is the five Lawless Islands (the client calls this area the "Savage Islands"), where players from different sides can fight. Whoever dies leaves loot for others to pick up. No law, no land claims — just high-level resources and the toughest animals in the game.

Sail to a Lawless Island once you reach level 56 Attack players who aren't in your party, clan or allied clan — area moves can hit several enemies at once Pick up the packages other players drop when they die Gather and hunt on a level 60 island (animals Lv55–65) Play last-one-standing matches on Brawl Island (level 50+) — see Brawl Island

Name shown in game   Climate เกาะไร้กฎ ภูเขาไฟ (Lawless Volcano)   Tropical เกาะไร้กฎ บึง (Lawless Swamp)   Tropical เกาะไร้กฎ ป่าเขตร้อน (Lawless Tropical Forest)   Tropical เกาะไร้กฎ ทุ่งหิมะ (Lawless Snowfield)   Temperate เกาะไร้กฎ ป่าอบอุ่น (Lawless Temperate Forest)   Temperate Island names are shown in Thai on this server, even in the English client. Island level 60 · Index 1 (no resistance needed) · no lifespan — they never disappear like Unstable Islands · island fatigue like a level 60 Unstable Island Wild animals are level 55–65 (island level ±5, like every level 60 island) — see Animals The terrain is the same as island 4 of the same climate (e.g. Volcano 4), but it's a separate island with its own resources No Domains · you can place temporary things (bonfires, camps), but they decay under the outside-a-Domain rules (Decay and repair)

At a Harbor → Sail → the sea map has 2 Lawless Island areas (tropical 3 islands · temperate 2 islands) Pick an island and confirm — if you have no clan, the confirm box warns "You can be attacked on … if you don't belong to a clan." You need level 56 or higher — below that you can't sail there · sailing is free Log out on a Lawless Island → you come back to the same place next time (if you're below level 56, you're moved to your home island)

You can hit: players who are not in your party, not in your clan and not in an allied clan — no clan = anyone can hit you How: tap an enemy player → Attack, or pick them as a target in combat mode — the same moves you use on animals (Combat) Hits don't land on: players who still have the Protection shield · dead players · players who are sailing away or logging out · other players' pets (pets don't attack players either) · buildings — a blocked hit shows as a miss, with a system message saying why (Thai-only) No safe zone from players — the 12-tile zone around the Harbor only keeps out animals On every other island you still can't hit players

The attacker's attack and armor penetration are set against the target's defense, as in when animals hit you, but the defense curve, the multipliers and the critical chance are a separate PvP set — hunting, animals hitting you and pets are unchanged. Damage = attack × move multiplier × armor penetration multiplier (table below) × direction multiplier × critical × kind-of-move multiplier × 0.5 The armor penetration multiplier depends on «attacker's armor penetration − target's net defense»; between the points of the table it is a straight line Penetration − defense   Multiplier −100 or lower   ×0.4545 −50   ≈ ×1.06 0   ×1.67 +14   ×1.77 +54   ×2.05 +117 or higher   ×2.2 As the target's defense rises, damage falls gradually, with no sudden jump — mid-tier armor still cuts some damage, high armor plus defense skills clearly help · defense more than 100 above the attacker's penetration doesn't help any further (floor ×0.4545) A move that rolls the «ignores defense» chance from a penetration skill is counted as if the target had 0 defense Kind-of-move multiplier (applied last, together with PvP's ×0.5, rounded once) Kind of move   Kind multiplier   With ×0.5 Melee (bare hands, one-handed, two-handed, spear — area moves included)   ×0.8   ×0.4 Ranged (bow, crossbow)   ×0.35   ×0.175 A swing with no move data (e.g. a catapult shot)   ×0.15   ×0.075 The ×0.5 is a test-period value — it makes up for our characters' lower HP (about 670–920 at Lv60) compared with the original game, and
When you log in or sail to a Lawless Island you get the Protection status for 30 seconds — other players can't hit you · it ends as soon as you move, warp or interact (attack, tap, gather)

Death and revival work like on every island (instant revive · CPR · respawn — Death & Revival); only the dropped items are different: Items drop when you press respawn, in the usual share (~50% of unlocked, unequipped items · the clan anti-drop buff still helps) — instant revive or CPR from a friend = nothing drops The dropped items become a package on the ground where you died that anyone can pick up, your killer included — it lasts 5 minutes Untradeable items don't go into the package — they stay in your own private pile, recovered as usual The victim sees the killer's name in system chat and on the timeline · the killer sees the victim's name No reward or exp for kills, only what drops

A last-one-standing match for up to 16 players from one server-wide queue — you go in bare-handed, gather and craft weapons on the island, anyone who dies is out, and the last survivor wins (the game calls it 난투섬 «Brawl Island») How to enter Level 50 or higher · open at all times · main menu → the banner «난투섬에 도전하라!» → press «난투섬 입장 등록» (cancel the queue with «등록 취소») — these menu texts are still in Korean in the game One queue for the whole server: with 4 players a 3-minute countdown starts (more players joining doesn't reset it · dropping below 4 cancels it), then everybody departs · with 16 players it departs at once You can't queue while in a party (leave it first), and you can't create, invite to or accept a party during a match · you can't sail or warp out mid-match — the only way out is the «나가기» button On the island One island per match, from 5 maps used in turn (tropical · temperate · volcanic · snow · swamp) · every match gets its own copy of the island No wild animals on Brawl Island (as on the original island) — the only enemies are other players Bare-handed: you use a separate bag that starts empty · your real bag is kept safe — nothing drops or is lost, and you get it all back when you leave (items gathered on the island don't come back with you) · skill EXP and quest progress earned on the island count for your real character The same fighting rules as the Lawless Islands (Who can hit whom · Damage) — clanmates and allied clans can't hit each other Dying means

What   Value Number of islands   5 Island level / level to enter   60 / 56 Damage multiplier against players (halving included)   Melee ×0.4 · ranged ×0.175 · penetration by table Base critical chance against players   4% Arrival shield   30 seconds Area move targets   Up to 6 per swing Death package   ~50% · lasts 5 minutes · anyone can pick it up

[!warn] Without a clan anyone can attack you, and strong moves can kill an unarmored player in a few hits — wear armor and lock your valuables in the bag before you go (locked items never drop). [!tip] Go with friends in the same party or clan — you can't hit each other, and your area moves never hit your own side.

d: Animal temperaments, counterattacks, island-based levels, herds and alphas, estates with no wild spawns, predators hunting prey, movement/sleep, and what you get from butchering — with the source animal's name

sec.x: Every island is home to herds of dinosaurs and prehistoric animals. Some attack the moment they see you, some run, some ignore you until they are hit. Animals have levels based on their island, sleep at night, hunt each other in front of you, and leave a carcass you can butcher for meat, leather and bones. Raptor Tyrannosaurus Sabertooth Mammoth

Hunt animals and butcher their carcasses into materials (see Combat) Capture animals to raise as pets (see Taming) Challenge the alpha of each island Watch predators hunt prey · sneak past animals sleeping at night

Temperament   Behavior Aggressive   Sees you within 8 tiles (closer if you have Stealth) → notices you in 2.5 seconds (alphas 1.5) → roars and chases · gives up once more than 32 tiles from home Neutral   Ignores you until hit, then fights back Skittish   Runs away when hit or when a predator comes After 20 seconds out of combat, animals regenerate 0.3% health per second · Tyrannosaurus and Apatosaurus regenerate 1% per second · Allosaurus does not regenerate Giving up the chase far from home doesn't mean you can hit it for free — an animal you're hitting will always strike back if it can reach you, see When an animal is hit [!tip] If you hit an animal and then leave it alone for a long time, it heals back — keep the pressure on when hunting big animals

sec.h: Compsognathus on Ancora and the Safe House
sec.x: Compsognathus — small green dinosaurs — roam in small herds of 3–4 close to where new players start, an easy first hunt Island   Herds   Where   Level Ancora (starting island)   3 herds   The bay beside the spawn valley · both banks of the stream (about 15–40 tiles from the spawn point)   1–6 Safe House   3 new herds + the old one   Around the landing point to the north, east and south-west (about 25–35 tiles away, never walking into the camp) · the old herd to the south-east   1–10 Harmless — they never chase or attack players and run away when hit · butchering gives meat and bones (see Butchering and drops) On Ancora they don't block the tutorial and aren't part of it · hunted herds slowly come back to the same spots The first time you take a Company hunting/butchering mission on the Safe House, 3 Compsognathus pop up around you for it (once per character — see Organizations) · animals that appear this way don't respawn after dying

Aggressive and neutral animals that get hit turn on whoever hit them — standing in a safe zone or luring them far from home won't let you hit them for free If it can reach you, it strikes back: if you've hit it within the last 20 seconds and you're inside its counter range (the reach of that species' longest attack + 1 tile), it hits back every time — even when lured more than 32 tiles from home, or when you're standing in a safe zone Far from home: more than 32 tiles from home it won't keep chasing — step out of its counter range and it gives up (you still can't lure it any farther) Safe zones (12-tile radius around Harbors and arrival points): animals never step inside — hit one from inside the zone and it runs up to the edge and strikes back if it can reach you If you stand deeper inside where it can't reach you, it roars a warning once and just watches (it doesn't swing attacks that can't land) After 10 seconds of not being able to reach you, it loses interest, walks back home and its health refills to full Idle, wandering animals avoid walking into safe zones · any already inside slowly walk out on their own Aggressive animals that spotted you and gave chase on their own (you haven't hit them) still give up when you enter a safe zone Skittish animals still run away when hit, as in the original game (no counterattack) · stunned/collapsed animals don't attack Hitting from somewhere the animal can't walk to (a small island or sandbar cut off by water, a cliff or mound it ca

Your Stealth Ability (on the stats window) makes aggressive animals spot you from closer, and sleeping animals wake only when you come closer than before · the distance is divided by the original game's formula, which divides by at most about 1.1 — in practice it is about 0.7 tiles shorter, and even a little Stealth gives nearly the full effect Stealth   Aggressive animals see you (sunny)   Rain   Heavy rain   Sleeping animals wake when you come within 0   8 tiles   6.4   4.8   4 tiles 24 (Stealth I–VI complete)   7.3 tiles   5.8   4.4   3.6 tiles Stealth comes from   Amount The Stealth I–VI skills   +4 per step (24 in total) Perception stat   every 6 points above 10 = +1 Gloomy Ambiance in a house (Buffs)   +25 Clan Research Ecology   +10 Some worn items and stealth attributes (Clothing)   Per item It does not affect animals that chase you back after being hit, nor predators hunting other animals [!tip] To sneak past animals sleeping at night, maxed-out Stealth lets you walk about 0.4 tiles closer (the effect is small)

Every animal spawns at island level ±5 (minimum 1) — including alphas, elite leaders and animals guarding resource caches/rifts · so low-level islands no longer have alphas far above the island's level · for high-level islands see High-level islands Animals reborn into a herd (after dying or being captured) roll a new level in this range each time Health, attack and defense grow with level using the original game's formula (health ≈ species constant × (level + 24)²) The same species at different levels can differ a lot in toughness — that is real game data, not a bug Animal   Lv10   Lv20   Lv30   Lv60 Raptor (health)   488   817   —   — Sabertooth (health)   1,053   1,764   2,656   6,428

There is no special rule for high-level islands right now — every animal on them spawns at island level ±5 like anywhere else (no animals above Lv65) Island level   Animal level 55   50–60 60 (the highest island level)   55–65 The highest islands that exist right now are level 55 and level 60 · so a level-60 island can have Lv61–65 animals, above the character level cap (60) Health, attack and defense grow with level using the same formula (see the table above) You can capture animals above level 60 and bond them as pets — see Taming

On an Unstable Island the health and attack of every animal (alphas included) are multiplied by 1 + (Unstable Index − 1) × 0.25 · the level shown over its head does not change Unstable Index   1   3   4   7   10 Multiplier   ×1   ×1.5   ×1.75   ×2.5   ×3.25

Public islands hold 6–12 animals per 64×64-tile area depending on terrain (see below), living in herds of up to 6 animals, using the species from that island's table Every island keeps at least 3 herds with ≥ 3 animals each — if hunting drops it below that, the missing herd returns to its spot after 3 minutes (aggressive) · 2 minutes (skittish) · 4 minutes (neutral) Safehouses, tutorial islands and peaceful islands are not topped up Each Unstable Island has the species and herds from its own table (original game + player tables), not the public-island set — alphas unchanged Areas with nobody around for 30 minutes put their herds to rest and set them up again when someone returns

How many animals live in each 64×64-tile area depends on the island's terrain: Terrain   Animals per area   Split into herds Grassland · savanna · tropical forest · temperate forest   12   2 herds × 6 Swamp · tundra · other terrain   9   a herd of 6 + a herd of 3 Snow islands · desert · volcanic   6   1 herd × 6 Areas that already hold more than this are not culled — they thin out naturally as animals are hunted or migrate The 3-herd minimum per island and the alphas are unchanged

A herd settling somewhere new (a herd moving in, or one added when an area opens) picks a random spot on land in the area at least 4 tiles from water and more than 8 tiles from any herd of the same species — herds no longer pile up on the shore or at the edge of the area If more than 6 animals of the same species are within 8 tiles of each other, the extras get split off: A predator nearby (within 16 tiles) → the closest one hunts the extras right away, without waiting to get hungry · the ones it kills are reborn in another herd of that species that isn't full, or at a new home (not back in the same pile) No predator → the extras move off to a new home on their own Alphas, elite leaders, fixed-spot animals, storage/rift guards and players' pets don't count · moves stay inside the same 64×64-tile area

sec.h: No wild animals spawn on player estates
sec.x: Wild animals do not spawn or settle on player, clan and personal-island estates, nor in a 12-tile band around the edge of an estate Animals whose home is already inside that area are moved out — silently if nobody is watching, otherwise they walk out to a new home (ones that are fighting, chasing, stunned, being hunted or eating wait for the next pass) A herd that is reborn after deaths comes back at the herd's old home, not wherever an animal chasing a player happens to be standing Walking in isn't blocked — an animal that is chasing a player can still follow into the estate · fixed-spot animals, rift/storage guards and animals spawned by missions are not covered A new or expanded estate takes effect within a few seconds

Wild herds don't stay put forever — in areas where players are present: Herds that are still whole move away from time to time (about 10–30 minutes, random per herd · one herd per area at a time) — they walk away from people toward the edge and vanish once they are at least 23 tiles from every player, then a new herd settles at a random spot in the area (appearing out of sight and walking in), which may be a species you've never seen there A herd that fails to leave (someone keeps following it or fighting it for too long) gives up and returns to its old home A herd that is wiped out is not replaced by a new herd — its members are reborn into the same herd one by one, see Population recovery · the exception is a herd wiped out while it was leaving: a new herd moves in after about 20 minutes Sleeping herds can migrate without walking (they vanish when nobody is nearby) Areas with nobody around don't rotate · returning to an area you left for a long time rotates it once when you get back Areas never hold more animals than the numbers by terrain Never migrate: alphas/elite leaders · fixed-spot animals · animals guarding storages or rifts · animals that are fighting, chasing, being hunted, dazed or eating a carcass · no migration on Tamed Islands, safehouses or peaceful islands

Most islands have one alpha per alpha species (e.g. the Alpha Tyrannosaurus). Alphas are always aggressive and never sleep Topic   Value Health   ×2.5 of the same species (at least 2,000 + 50 × level) Elite leaders   ×1.5 (at least 250 + 12 × level) Respawn at the same spot   30 minutes (elite leaders 10 minutes) EXP for the kill   ×4 of a normal animal of the same level (elite leaders ×1.8) Examples   Alpha Tyrannosaurus Lv60 ≈ 389,191 · Allosaurus Lv60 ≈ 96,914 · Elephantulus Lv60 = 5,000 Alphas and elite leaders are island level ±5 like every other animal (Animal levels) · so the Lv60 examples above show up on level-55 to level-60 islands No alphas on Tamed Islands or safehouses · on Unstable Islands their health is multiplied by the Index as well

On level-60 Unstable Islands, each resource cache around a crater has a guard animal — the species follows the original sheet for that cache (for example the cranberry grove on the snow island = Coelophysis · the agave grove in the desert = Tuojiangosaurus · the tropical gem mine = Kentrosaurus · the cattail grove in the swamp = Giant Rat) · its level follows island level ±5 and it gets the island's Unstable Index multiplier

In areas where players are present, hungry aggressive carnivores actually chase down other animals in front of you They only hunt neutral/skittish animals of a different species and no higher level · alphas neither hunt nor get hunted · players' pets are never hunted Skittish prey runs once the predator is within 8 tiles · neutral prey fights back After a kill the predator eats for 20 seconds, then rests from hunting for 10 minutes · it gives up a chase after 60 seconds The kill leaves a carcass you can butcher, but with half the meat (leather/bones are complete) · no EXP/quest credit since you didn't kill it Hit a predator mid-hunt and it turns on you · a predator already chasing you won't switch to hunting animals At most 2 hunts at a time per area · for when predators go hunting see Hunting when hungry · no hunting on peaceful islands

Each predator gets hungry every ~15 minutes on average (random 7.5–22.5 minutes per animal) and goes after nearby prey within 16 tiles A predator needs about 8 bites to kill its prey · big prey fights back harder, and the predator can lose Anything that dies in a hunt (prey or predator) is reborn into its herd one at a time, the same as any other death — see Population recovery · the carcass can still be butchered (half the meat) Still at most 2 hunts at a time per area · predators rest 10 minutes after eating · sleeping predators and those chasing a player don't hunt

Running: animals use their real run animation when chasing or fleeing (same speed as before, 0.925 tiles/second · walking 0.575) Sleeping: a game day lasts 48 minutes: dawn (4:30–8) · day (8–17) · dusk (17–21) · night (21–4:30) Night animals (wolves, sabertooths, etc.) are awake at dusk and night · everything else is awake except at night Outside its waking hours each animal has a 45% chance to be asleep (re-rolled daily) · sleeping animals don't wander, chase or hunt They wake if you come within 4 tiles (3 tiles with Stealth) or hit them, then stay awake for 2 minutes · alphas and water animals never sleep Flinching: every hit plays a short flinch (visual only) · only a critical hit or a full stagger gauge interrupts the attack an animal is winding up Roaring: aggressive animals roar the first time they spot you (standing still ≤ 2 seconds) before chasing · alphas roar when a fight starts · once per 60 seconds per animal · no damage · some species have no roar (Sabertooth, Mammoth, Allosaurus, etc.) Stunned/collapsed: see Taming [!tip] Gathering at night on islands with aggressive (non-nocturnal) animals is safer — just don't walk right next to a sleeping one

A dead animal leaves a carcass for 15 minutes (each butchering resets the timer) Tap the carcass → choose a part to butcher, one piece at a time until it's empty · parts you haven't unlocked with butchering skills are greyed out Item level = animal level + your Butchering skill bonus, but never above your character level Animal   Carcass parts (per carcass) Compsognathus   Meat 1–2 · Carnivore Leg Bone 1–2 · Leather 1 · Teeth 1 Raptor   Meat 2–3 · Carnivore Leg Bone 1–2 · Leather 1–2 · Teeth 1 Triceratops   Meat 5–8 · Herbivore Rib 2–3 · Skull 1 · Horn 1–2 · Leather 2–3 · Large Leg Bone 2–3 Mammoth   Meat 7–10 · Herbivore Leg Bone 2–3 · Herbivore Rib 2–3 · Skull 1 · Ivory 1–2 · Pelt 2–3 · Fat 1–2 · Large Leg Bone 2–3 · Intestine 1–2 Tyrannosaurus   Meat 8–12 · Carnivore Leg Bone 3–4 · Carnivore Rib 3–4 · Large Skull 1 · Leather 3–4 · Teeth 1 · Large Leg Bone 1–2 Parts that were broken when the animal died give half (meat excluded) · carcasses left by predators give half the meat

Newly butchered materials (leather, meat, bones, teeth…) and materials from animals caught in traps carry the name of the animal they came from, for example «Tyrannosaurus Leather», «Ankylosaurus Rib», «Mammoth Pelt» — named by the animal's drop table as in the original game (a Chasmosaurus uses the Bonusaurus table, so it gives «Bonusaurus Horn») You can search the market by animal name (typing «Tyranno» finds Tyrannosaurus Leather) Each species passes its own species traits to its materials, and some pieces unlock recipes that used to be impossible: Brachio Tooth Necklace · White Wolf Fur Hat (dried White Direwolf leather) · tanning with White Sabertooth oil · Compy Beanbag · Andrewsarchus Leather Rug Compsognathus now also drop 1 leather and 1 tooth, and Brachiosaurus drop 1–2 teeth (this lets those recipes be crafted) Processed materials keep their usual names · old items in your bag with no animal data keep their old neutral name — nothing is guessed after the fact Parts from trapped animals get the name, the species traits and the yellow/green tag rolls just like animals you butcher yourself The names you will see in game (same table as above): Animal   Carcass parts (per carcass) Compsognathus   Compsognathus Meat 1–2 · Compsognathus Leg Bone 1–2 · Compsognathus Leather 1 · Compsognathus Tooth 1 Raptor   Raptor Meat 2–3 · Raptor Leg Bone 1–2 · Raptor Leather 1–2 · Raptor Tooth 1 Triceratops   Triceratops Meat 5–8 · Triceratops Rib 2–3 · Triceratops Skull 1 · Triceratop

Herd animals that die — killed by a player, eaten by a predator, captured or caught in a trap — don't pop back right away; they are reborn into the same herd one at a time: Wait = about 3.3 minutes × the number of animals the herd is missing (20 minutes ÷ 6) — missing 1 waits 3.3 minutes · missing 2 waits 6.7 minutes · … · a whole herd of 6 wiped out waits 20 minutes before the first one returns After each birth the timer restarts based on how many are still missing · more deaths while waiting restart it too — so small remnants come back slowly, and a wiped-out herd of 6 takes about 70 minutes to fill up again If players are nearby, the newcomer appears out of sight (at least 23 tiles from every player, on the herd's side) and walks into the herd · with nobody around it appears right in the herd Alphas/elite leaders respawn on their own timers (Alphas) · the 3-herds-per-island minimum always applies

d: Only some species can be captured — beat an animal below 30% health or stun it, then capture it with a Taming Herb, and tame it in a pen for 1 hour before forming a bond

sec.x: Some wild animals can become your companion (Animals you can capture). The steps are weaken it → capture it with a Taming Herb → get its Rein → tame it in a pen → form a bond, and you get a pet that travels with you, can be ridden, helps in fights and produces goods. Capturing an animal and putting it in a pen

Capture a wild animal at ≤ 30% health or while it is stunned/collapsed (any health) Use blunt weapons or heavy moves to stun animals faster Tame captured animals in a taming pen, then bond with them as pets

You can only capture the species the original game lets you tame — and you must first learn that species' capture skill (Survival category, «Animal Handling» line) · if you haven't, the server opens the skill window for you; there is no bar and the tool is not worn Survival category level needed   Animals you can capture 15   Zebraceratops · Protoceratops (including the light pink one) 20   Oviraptor · Albiraptor · Pictaraptor · Macrauchenia · Deinonychus 30   Raptor · Coelophysis (including the snowfield one) 35   Male Megaloceros (including the white-bellied one) · Pavomimus 40   Skunkodus 45   Styracosaurus · Centrosaurus 50   Ornithomimus 60   Dilophosaurus Needs both: the capture skill + a clan that has done the research — Ankylosaurus · Direwolf · Jungle Sabertooth ① Learn that species' capture skill: Ankylosaurus = Capturing Quadrupedal Dinos II (Survival category Lv45) · Direwolf / Jungle Sabertooth = Capturing Combative Mammals II (Survival category Lv60) ② Be in a clan that has researched «Research Advanced Capture», with the buff still active — researched at the Quality Research Center for 150,000 T Stone · the buff lasts 2 hours · it can be researched again 6 hours after it ends (Clan research) ③ No clan, or the clan hasn't researched it / the buff has run out = no capture button at all when you tap the animal (the game shows no message), even if you have learned the skill The black Direwolf (Lawless Island) has no capture skill, so it can't be captured Some sub-v

Item   Level   Used for Novice Taming Herb   1–19   Capture tool — must be in your bag Standard Taming Herb   20–39   〃 Advanced Taming Herb   40–60   〃 Makeshift Taming Pen / Small Taming Pen   —   Taming the animals you capture The capture tool loses 3 durability per capture attempt (success or not) · pressing capture before the animal qualifies does not wear the tool

Hit the animal until it has ≤ 30% health or until it is stunned/collapsed (see the stun gauge below) Target it and press Capture  — the button works once you have a tool and have learned that species' capture skill (it doesn't wait for low health); the server checks the conditions Stand still for the 3-second bar (moving cancels) Success → the animal leaves the world and its Rein goes into your bag · failure → a message shows the chance that was rolled; try again after the 5-second cooldown If it doesn't qualify yet, a server message (in Thai) tells you to get its health below 30% or stun it first Carcasses and rift guardians can't be captured · you must stand close · some species can't be captured at all (button locked) [!tip] If you walk away from a low-health animal it can heal back above 30% (it regenerates 20 seconds after combat) — capture quickly

sec.h: When your animal slots are full
sec.x: If you already own as many animals as your limit allows (8 to start with), pressing Capture shows a server message (in Thai) that your animals are full right away — no bar, no tool wear · set one roaming on your Tamed Island or set one free first, then capture again · Reins you have not bonded yet don't count — details in Pets

Chance = level factor × (1 − 0.8 × (remaining health ÷ max health)²) · always between 2% and 98% The level factor comes from (your character level + Capture Ability ÷ 10) − the animal's level; the higher it is, the easier · 6 or more levels below the animal = 2% Being stunned/collapsed only allows capture at high health — the chance still uses the real health, with no extra bonus Level used − animal   Health 0%   10%   30%   Stunned, 50% health   Stunned, 80% health   Stunned, full health −6   2%   2%   2%   2%   2%   2% −3   50%   50%   46%   40%   24%   10% 0   80%   79%   74%   64%   39%   16% +3   93%   92%   86%   74%   45%   19% +5   97%   96%   90%   77%   47%   19% +10   98%   98%   92%   80%   49%   20%

Every 10 points of Capture Ability (on the stats window) count as 1 extra character level when the capture chance is worked out Comes from   Amount Capture skills (Capturing Bipedal/Quadrupedal Dinos · Capturing Mammals, etc. — 10 steps)   +4 to +7 per step (55 in total) Clan Research Ecology   +5 Example: a level 20 character capturing an animal at 30% health Animal   No Capture Ability   15   35   55 (all skills) Lv20   74%   82%   87%   90% Lv25   17%   40%   63%   77% Lv30   2%   2%   2%   25% [!note] The in-game hint says the capture tool's level matters, but on this server the chance uses your character level (plus Capture Ability) against the animal's level

Every animal has a stun gauge (for small animals it is roughly 2× their health · multiplied by the island's Unstable Index). Each hit drains it, and the animal moves through these stages Stage   Gauge left   Effect   In-game message Weakened   ≤ ⅓   Warning message only   "… is losing strength." Stunned   ≤ ⅑   Frozen: no attacks, no walking, no fleeing · the attack it was winding up is cancelled   "… is stunned." Collapsed   0   Falls down with stars over its head   "… collapsed!" Recovered   time runs out   Gauge full again   "… steadied itself." A heavy hit can skip from weakened straight to collapsed · you can capture at any moment while it's stunned/collapsed When the fight ends (the animal gives up or returns home) the gauge silently refills · the gauge does not recover by itself mid-fight Animal   Stunned for (seconds)   Collapsed for (seconds) Compsognathus · Phenacodus   6   6 Raptor · Direwolf   8   8 Sabertooth   10   10 Iguanodon   12   12 Triceratops · Mammoth   4   6 Tyrannosaurus   5   3

Gauge drained per hit = damage dealt × the move's stun value × direction (front/back ×1.25 · sides ×1) × (1 + skill bonus) × 4 Move   Stun value Bow/crossbow normal shot · quick/aimed shot   0.3 · 0.5 Bare hand · one-handed · two-handed (normal hit)   0.4 · 0.7 · 0.8 One-handed heavy hit · two-handed heavy hit   0.8 · 1.0 One-handed stab · two-handed strike   1.5 · 1.6 Blunt Weapon Specialization I–III +6% per level (blunt weapon moves) · Crossbow Specialization I–III +10% per level No drain from: your pet's attacks · bleeding · animals fighting each other · traps Hits needed to stun / collapse / kill (hitting from the front, weapon level = animal level · "dies first" = health runs out before that stage) Weapon   Raptor Lv10   Iguanodon Lv30 Bare Handed   Stunned 13 · dies 14 (dies before collapsing)   83 · 93 · 172 Stone Hammer   3 · 4 · 6   10 · 11 · 34 Two-Handed Stone Hammer strike + Blunt Weapon Specialization III   1 · 1 · 2   1 · 2 · 10 Mahogany Crossbow + Crossbow Specialization III   Dies before stun (dies at 6)   16 · 18 · 33 [!tip] For small animals use a hammer or other blunt weapon and hit from the front or back — they usually get stunned while still at 30–45% health, so you can capture before accidentally killing them

sec.h: After the capture: taming in a pen
sec.x: Taming pen Build/place a taming pen and put the Rein into it Start taming — it takes 1 hour (3,600 seconds for every species) · base success chance 60% (maximum 100%) Feed it during taming to help: Food   Effect All-Purpose Taming Feed   Chance +10% · time −30% Fast Taming Feed   Time −50% Meat / Minnow   Time −10 seconds per piece When time is up, collect the result: success → the animal is tamed and gets a random rank (S · A · B · C · D, whichever that species can have — the rank sets how many property slots it has, see Pets) · failure → the animal escapes to the wild and the Rein is lost Use the tamed animal's Rein to form a bond → it becomes your pet (the Rein's level must not exceed your Survival category level) — continue at Pets Taming time can't be cut below half [!note] Animal traps give carcass items (meat, leather, bones), not live animals to raise

Level-60 islands can have wild animals of Lv61–65 (Wild animals) — you can capture them as usual The Rein you get shows at most level 60 (the Rein level cap) even if the animal is higher — so you can form a bond once your Survival category level reaches 60 · the animal itself keeps its real level If your Survival category is below the Rein's level, the game won't let you form the bond and the server also refuses with a message (in Thai) saying the animal's level is above your Survival level · the Rein stays in your bag Pets above level 60 can't level up further with EXP (pet level cap 60) — see Pets

d: Summon pets to fight on their own, ride and carry items, feed them, unlock properties on the wheel, use their active skills, produce milk in pens, revive them and keep them from aging — max level 60

sec.x: Animals you capture and tame become your pets once you form a bond. Summon them to follow you, ride them, carry items in their bag, let them help in fights on their own or with their active skill, or put them in a pen to produce milk or train for levels. A bonded pet

Summon / return — one at a time · animals in a pen or roaming can't be summoned · a knocked-out pet can be summoned but only as a body that must be revived first (Revival) Ride — rideable species only (speed depends on species, e.g. Raptor 700 · Mammoth 160) Animal bag — slots depend on species, e.g. Raptor 10 · Sabertooth 30 · Ankylosaurus 150 · Triceratops 240 · Mammoth 300 · Brachiosaurus 500 Feed to restore vigor · rename (1–16 characters) · set free (the animal is gone forever · items in its bag go back to your bag) Roaming — let animals roam your Tamed Island · there are 5 roaming slots and you can buy more with the «Roaming Expansion Ticket», 30 Durango Coins per slot (up to 13 purchases = 18 slots in total · slots are counted per character) · roaming animals don't age, can't produce or train, and items in their bag disappear Fight on their own when you are in combat mode — see Pets that fight for you Unlock properties on the wheel as the pet levels up, and draw an active skill at level 60 — see Property wheel · Active skills Reset rank (needs a «Rank Reset Ticket», earned from events) — you see the rolled rank first, then accept it or keep the old one · accepting the new rank wipes all properties and the active skill, and the number of property slots follows the new rank Break the bond (turn the pet back into a Rein) needs one «Animal Bond-Breaker Ticket» (used up) — species that can't be un-bonded can't

sec.h: How many animals you can own
sec.x: Skill   Maximum owned animals None   8 Animal Handling I / II / III / IV   9 / 10 / 11 / 12 [!note] The skill descriptions in the game still say «total 10/12/14/16» but this server gives +1 per level (as in the original sheet) — the real numbers are 9 / 10 / 11 / 12 The pet window and the top bar show «count / maximum» Counted: summoned animals, stored animals, animals in a pen · not counted: animals roaming your Tamed Island, and Reins you have not bonded yet Once full you can't capture wild animals, bond Reins or bring a roaming animal back — a message tells you, tools don't wear and the Reins stay in your bag · set one roaming or set one free first Swapping one for one (send 1 roaming, bring 1 back) always works, even when full If you already own more than the limit, none of your animals disappear — you just can't add more until you are below the limit The pet window's button for bringing a roaming animal back now works

Reins from animal packages (sold in the Shop) hold an already tamed animal — press Form a Bond from your bag right away, no pen needed · its rank is rolled the same way as a successful pen taming · full health and fullness · 60-day lifespan · it still counts toward how many animals you can own

A pet's vigor (300 max for every species) drops only while it is summoned, and is used for fighting, skills and production Species   Vigor lost per second   Full to empty Raptor · Direwolf · Oviraptor · Ornithomimus, etc. (18 species)   0.05   ~100 minutes All other species (83)   0.09   ~55 minutes Food   Vigor restored Leaf · Minnow   40 Meat   50 Nutritious Animal Feed   500 Highly Nutritious Animal Feed   700 Infinite Vigor Feed   Vigor stops dropping for a while Only animal food can be fed (the feeding menu lists it) · a full pet can't eat normal food (food that carries property values can still be fed when full) Herbivores can eat only herbivore food and carnivores only carnivore food — feeding the wrong kind shows a warning and nothing is used up · all-purpose food (for example Shop feed, medicine) works for both Food with property values (fed inside a pen or from your bag) raises the odds of those properties on the wheel — see Property wheel Attack and Provoke skills, and fighting on their own, need at least half of max vigor (150)

A pet's health, attack and defense come from the original stat table (health = species constant × (level + 24)²) · the defense shown on the pet screen is the same value that reduces damage when it is hit · pets regenerate 0.3% health per second Max health can be raised by properties and skill buffs — the bar really gets longer, but the extra health is not filled in at once If wild animals bring it to 0 health the pet falls and stays as a body in the world · you can summon a fallen pet (the body appears next to you) but can't ride it, use its skills or have it fight until it is revived Revive: tap the fallen pet and choose the revive menu (in the Thai game the menu is named «บันทึก») or press the revive button  on the pet screen → full health, vigor at least half · free, no medicine needed Example stats for level-60 pets (species that aren't in the original table use the closest profile, e.g. Tyrannosaurus uses Tarbosaurus · aged pets have half the stats): Species   Health   Attack   Defense Raptor · Oviraptor · Pictaraptor · Deinonychus   1,323   63   240 Direwolf · Sabertooth · Dilophosaurus · Ornithomimus · Pavomimus · Megaloceros   2,941   84   240 Ankylosaurus   8,820   252   360 Deinotherium (small elephant from the Shop)   13,230   252   270 Tarbosaurus   17,640   336   550

A pet captured in the wild lives for 30 days from bonding · pets from the Shop, gifts or (some) event animals live 60 days — then they show as "Old" and their stats are halved (health, health regen, attack, defense, speed, bag, max vigor, accuracy, etc.) An old pet can't start new production or training in a pen (a job already running finishes) Roaming on your Tamed Island stops the aging clock Animal Anti-Aging Remedy (15/30/45/60 days) gives life time back, but never beyond the full lifespan

When you are in combat mode (you hit an animal, or an animal hits you into combat mode), your summoned pet joins the fight by itself — nothing to press Target = the one you selected (none selected = whoever is hitting you) · it stops when you leave combat mode or the target dies · the target must be within 15 tiles of you The pet plays its species' real attack moves (lunging/jumping when the target is a little farther away) · damage = the pet's attack through the same penetration formula as Combat · it walks around deep water or cliffs to stand and fight, and doesn't join if it can't reach the target Wild animals compete for a target: a wild animal remembers the damage you and your pet did to it (the pet's damage is multiplied by that species' value — Ankylosaur land tortoise ×3, all others ×1) and goes after whichever side did more · a pet takes full damage by the formula and can be knocked out (Revival) Conditions: pet summoned, not knocked out, not in a pen, not being ridden · a species that can fight (a few ornamental ones such as the Labrador or fancy Phenacodus can't) · vigor at least half to join, then it keeps fighting until vigor runs out (fighting costs no extra vigor) · you are not standing in water EXP: a summoned pet (not knocked out, not in a pen or roaming) gets 20% of the EXP your character earns from every source (hunting, gathering, etc.) — even a level-60 character at the cap still gives the pet 20% of the EXP it would have earned Pets don't hit players, an

Each pet has property slots set by its rank — the higher the rank, the more slots — and each slot opens when the pet reaches a set level Rank   Slots   Opens at pet level S   5   20 · 30 · 40 · 50 · 60 A   4   20 · 30 · 40 · 60 B   3   20 · 40 · 60 C   2   30 · 60 D   1   60 When the level is reached the pet discovers a property — the wheel spins and rolls one tag, then you accept it or spin again (the «Attribute Discovery Rate» page shows each tag's odds) · tags raise the pet's stats, for example speed, attack, defense, bag size, vigor, max health, health regen, accuracy and production amount The wheel has a «No Ability» slot of about 20% — landing on it means that step passes without a tag, but you get a consolation item in your bag (by mail if your bag is full) · you can spin again as usual Spin again in the same step with T Stone depending on the pet's level — the first respin costs about 797 (level 20) · 1,436 (30) · 2,454 (40) · 3,898 (50) · 5,805 (60) and gets more expensive every time (the 2nd at level 20 ≈ 906) — or use a respin ticket · a tag you already hold is not rolled again (the «No Ability» slot can repeat) Feeding food that carries property values raises that tag's odds on the wheel (its slice gets bigger and an up-arrow appears in the list page) — feeding inside a pen or from your bag both count, and the stored amount resets when you accept a property The 4 pet stamina tags were removed from the wheel (they had no effect in game) All slots opened + level 60

Each pet has 1 active skill (in the game they are called «special behaviors») out of 37 skill sets · strength follows the skill's rank C–S How you get one — the pet must be level 60 with all property slots opened (Property wheel) before you can draw a skill · the first draw is free · redrawing costs 100 Warp Gems, +100 more each time up to 1,000 (or use a redraw ticket) · a redraw may give the same skill again · the result depends on the species and the properties it has (species without a skill of their own get a general skill), and every species can draw Type   Examples   Effect Attack   Bite · Rush · Back Kick · Chemical Warfare   The pet plays the skill's real move on the target you're fighting (it runs or lunges up to 6 tiles to reach it) · damage per hit = the pet's attack ×2 · area moves hit everything in the area Provoke   Provoke   Wild animals within 3.5 tiles around the pet go after the pet instead of you Buff   Bared Fangs · Run Free · Strong Back · Healing Helper · Pack Mule   Temporarily raises your pet's or your own stats — the effects in the description really work (for example the pet's max health, slower vigor loss, or less energy spent when you gather or build) Skills work while the pet is summoned · each use costs 20 vigor · cooldown depends on the skill and rank (e.g. Bite 12–15 s · Provoke 30–33 s · Strong Back 300 s) A skill works only in its own situation: attack and provoke skills in combat mode · some buffs outside combat, some while riding — pressin

A pet and a pen Put a pet in an animal pen (Makeshift Pen · Small Pen · Medium Pen) → choose the pet → Production or Training → wait for the timer, then collect items and pet EXP Production / Training   Time   Vigor used   Pet EXP (production / training)   Unlocks at pet level Lv.1   1 h   150   40 / 100   1 Lv.2   2 h   170   110 / 270   10 Lv.3   4 h   190   290 / 700   20 Lv.4   8 h   270   1,100 / 2,700   30 Lv.5   10 h   460   3,900 / 9,700   40 Lv.6   12 h   590   15,000 / 38,000   50 Milk comes from production by mammal pets such as Phenacodus, Macrauchenia, Female Megaloceros, Direwolf, Skunkodus: each round gives Milk or Animal Droppings, 50% each Male Megaloceros only gives Animal Droppings · Bumblebee Phenacodus gives Honey 50% / Milk 30% / Animal Droppings 20% Amount per round = (2 + pet level ÷ 10) × the production level's multiplier (1 · 5/3 · 7/3 · 10/3 · 14/3 · 6), rounded down — a Lv1 pet on Production Lv.1 gives 2 · properties for production amount add to it, as shown on the pet screen 9–17% chance of a bonus item (coin · worm · corn seed) · item level = pet level Training gives the pet EXP in the second number of each cell (no items) and takes the same time and vigor as production of the same level Production/Training Lv.5–6 needs more than 300 vigor, so raise your pet's max vigor first · an old pet can't start a job [!tip] You can feed pets inside the pen (feed button on the pen screen) — top up vigor before starting a new production round

Pets can level up to 60 with pet EXP — from production and training in pens, from helping in fights, and from 20% of the EXP your character earns (Pets that fight for you) You can form a bond when your Survival category level reaches the Rein's level · Reins show at most level 60 (Animals above level 60) — a player whose Survival category is 60 can bond animals of any level A wild animal captured on a level-60 island may be Lv61–65 — that pet keeps its level but can't level up further with EXP

The first time you go to your Tamed Island you pick 1 of 5 maps (can't be changed afterwards) — see Choosing your Tamed Island layout · Tamed Islands are safe islands with no wild animals at all (no bosses) — to capture animals you have to go to other islands

d: The 8 basic abilities and what each one gives, max Health/Energy/Fatigue, combat stats, crafting/gathering stats, resistances and power ratings — where they come from, how they're calculated, which ones really matter

sec.x: The character info screen shows many values — the numbers it shows are now the same values the server really uses, counting every source (skills · titles · gear and tags · food · house ambiance · buffs and status effects such as personal/clan research, buffs from pets, event buffs). This page explains where each one comes from, how it's calculated and what it does on this server. When a buff or house ambiance runs out, your stats go back right away · negative statuses (e.g. the death penalty) really lower your stats too Value   Comes from   Affects 8 basic abilities   Character level + skill category levels + title + food/gear   Each one turns into several abilities, e.g. Endurance → max Health · Will → max Energy (table) Max Health / Energy · regen per second   Base + level + basic abilities + bonuses from every source   The on-screen gauges (Survival) Combat stats   The weapon and gear you wear + character bonuses (including the values from basic abilities) · skill effects on moves   Damage dealt and taken · auto-dodge/auto-block (Combat) Crafting / gathering stats   Character level + learned skills + values from basic abilities + bonuses from every source   Mastery ladder · craft success chance (Crafting · Gathering) Climate resistance   Time spent on islands of each climate + gear   Entry gates for high-Index islands · less weather fatigue (Weather) 3 power ratings   Weighted from the values above   Display only
